**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
[born of the bones of the earth](/Epithets.aspx?ID=7) or [restless as the tides](/Epithets.aspx?ID=11)

</column>

---

You churn the sea and fish up stone so your enemies together can receive their punishment. Each enemy in a 30-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or be swept up to 15 feet to another location of your choice within the affected area and become [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of your next turn. Then, if you’re on a surface, a pillar of earth rises underneath you and lasts for 1 minute. The pillar is 10 feet tall, and its surface includes your space and a 5-foot emanation around you. After the pillar rises, you can attempt a melee Strike against one enemy in reach.

---

You raise a druidic monument, such as a standing stone or warding tree, from the ground, creating a powerful primal ward that blocks other types of magic. The monument appears in an unoccupied square on the ground within 30 feet, making that square difficult terrain. Choose arcane, divine, or occult; all creatures within 15 feet of the monument gain a +2 status bonus to their saving throws against effects with that trait. The monument lasts for 1 round before crumbling back into the earth or wilting away into nothingness, but you can Sustain the monument for up to 1 minute.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Kitsune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=341" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 125

**Prerequisites**
[Change Shape](/Actions.aspx?ID=701) with a fox alternate form

</column>

---

Once per day, when you Change Shape into a fox, you can instead gain the effects of both the canine form of 5th-level [_animal form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=10) and 7th-level [_fiery body_](/Spells.aspx?ID=115) for 1 minute or until you shift back, whichever comes first. You can cast [_produce flame_](/Spells.aspx?ID=236) from the fiery body effect even though you're in a battle form.

**Special** If you are a [frozen wind kitsune](/Heritages.aspx?ID=139), your form is ice instead of fire. This changes the immunity and damage from the _fiery body_ effect to cold, changes the weakness to fire, and changes _produce flame_ to [_ray of frost_](/Spells.aspx?ID=245)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Evolution" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=394" />
<trait label="Summoner" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=392" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 68

</column>

---

Spines, flame jets, and holy blasts are just some of the ways your eidolon might strike from a distance. It gains a ranged [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack with a [range increment](/Traits.aspx?ID=248) of 30 feet that deals 1d4 damage and has the [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103) and [propulsive](/Traits.aspx?ID=191) traits. When you select this feat, choose a damage type: acid, bludgeoning, cold, electricity, fire, negative, piercing, positive, or slashing. If your eidolon is a [celestial](/Traits.aspx?ID=23), [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=70), or [monitor](/Traits.aspx?ID=111) with an alignment other than true neutral, you can choose a damage type in its alignment.

You become trained in ranger class DC. You can use the Hunt Prey action. Special You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the ranger archetype. Action Hunt Prey Single Action Concentrate Ranger Source Core Rulebook pg. 168 You designate a single creature as your prey and focus your attacks against that creature. You must be able to see or hear the prey, or you must be tracking the prey during exploration. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks when you Seek your prey and a +2 circumstance bonus to Survival checks when you Track your prey. You also ignore the penalty for making ranged attacks within your second range increment against the prey you’re hunting. You can have only one creature designated as your prey at a time. If you use Hunt Prey against a creature when you already have a creature designated, the prior creature loses the designation and the new prey gains the designation. Your designation lasts until your next daily preparations. Ranger Dedication leads to... Basic Hunter's Trick, Master Spotter (Ranger), Ranger Resiliency

    right="Feat 9"
    pfs=""
>
[Rapid Retraining](/Feats.aspx?ID=5258) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Reincarnated" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=783" />
<trait label="Universal Ancestry" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=467" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #199: To Bloom Below the Web](/Sources.aspx?ID=225) pg. 80

</column>

---

Some feel trapped by their choices and have a tough time reinventing themselves. To you, this dilemma is just a natural part of reincarnation. Retraining other feats or skill increases during downtime only takes 4 days instead of a week, and class features that require a choice can be retrained in a week instead of a month. You also never need to find a teacher to retrain, as the memories of abilities you possessed in past lives are superior to any instructor.

---

Your ability to curl up into a tight ball comes in handy. You roll up into a ball and move up to four times your Speed in a straight line down an incline. If you reach the bottom of the incline or hit an obstacle during this first turn of movement, you stop rolling safely. Otherwise, you automatically keep rolling at this Speed during subsequent turns until you hit the bottom of the incline or an obstacle ends this movement (which can happen in the middle of your turn). You're [slowed 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) each turn after the first that you keep rolling, and if you hit an obstacle on a turn after the first, you and the obstacle both take 4d6 bludgeoning damage and you stop rolling.

Striking the ground with the gravity of the deepest rocks, you cause an earthquake. This has the effects of [_earthquake_](/Spells.aspx?ID=95) but comes from you, with an area of a 60-foot cone or an emanation with the same size as your kinetic aura. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 290

**Archetype** [Razmiran Priest](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=307)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37); Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38)

</column>

---

You have earned entry to the priesthood of Razmir, either at the Exalted Lodge or another temple where Razmir’s holy masks are forged. You gain a [Razmiri mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3593) and can [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=2385) a replacement in 4 hours if yours is ever damaged or lost. There is no value in selling your Razmiri mask, and only you gain its benefits. The abilities of your Razmiri mask use the higher of your class DC or spell DC.

You can take the [Cleric Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5066) feat without needing to meet its prerequisites and before you take two other feats from the Razmiran priest archetype, but you must choose [Razmir](/Deities.aspx?ID=357) as your deity. All spells granted by the cleric archetype when gained in this way are [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) spells instead of [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spells, and cleric feats that normally have the [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579) trait instead have the [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662) trait. Your key spellcasting attribute for these spells is Charisma, rather than Wisdom.

<title level="2">Razmiran Priest Dedication leads to...</title>
[Living God](/Feats.aspx?ID=7570), [Mask of The 12th Step](/Feats.aspx?ID=7568), [Mask of The 15th Step](/Feats.aspx?ID=7569), [Perfect Truths](/Feats.aspx?ID=7567)

You gain a Razmiri mask and can Craft a replacement in 4 hours if yours is ever damaged or lost. There is no value in selling your Razmiri mask, and only you gain its benefits. The abilities of your Razmiri mask use the higher of your class DC or spell DC. You can take the Cleric Dedication feat without needing to meet its prerequisites and before you take two other feats from the Razmiran priest archetype, but you must choose Razmir as your deity. All spells granted by the cleric archetype when gained in this way are occult spells instead of divine spells, and cleric feats that normally have the divine trait instead have the occult trait. Your key spellcasting attribute for these spells is Charisma, rather than Wisdom. Razmiran Priest Dedication leads to... Living God, Mask of The 12th Step, Mask of The 15th Step, Perfect Truths

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #166: Despair on Danger Island](/Sources.aspx?ID=85) pg. 79

**Archetype** [Ghost Eater](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=92)

**Prerequisites**
[Ghost Eater Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2710)

</column>

---

You've learned to move your spiritual energy past yourself to attack spirits where others can't. You can make melee Strikes against [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) creatures that are inside solid objects as long as the object is within your reach. An incorporeal creature inside of a solid object is [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22), requiring you to succeed at a DC 11 flat check when you target it. You can spend an action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait, to focus on a creature inside of a solid object. If you do, the next melee Strike you make this turn requires you to succeed at only a DC 6 flat check to affect the creature.

    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"

[Reach for Immortality](/Feats.aspx?ID=7193) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Exemplar" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=839" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 43

**Frequency**
once per day

</column>

---

Your divine spark is now a bonfire in your soul, bringing you to the very cusp of undying immortality. You cease aging. When you would die for any reason, you can Spark Transcendence as a free action that can be taken at any time, regardless of your current condition. You reach for your divine spark and seize it in your hand to survive at 0 Hit Points, purging yourself of any negative conditions. Invigorated by this return to life, you then heal yourself for half of your total Hit Points, Stand, instantly summon any held ikons to your hand, and Shift your Immanence to any of your ikons.

>
[Reach for the Sky](/Feats.aspx?ID=3256) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=16" />
<trait label="Visual" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=163" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 136

**Archetype** [Pistol Phenom](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=120)

**Prerequisites**
[Pistol Phenom Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3251)

**Requirements**
You're wielding a loaded firearm.

</column>

---

You command the room, firing a gun into the air and ordering everyone to surrender and put their hands in the air. You fire your firearm and then attempt a single [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) check to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) each enemy within 30 feet. Creatures who become [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) instinctively put their hands in the air. If they had Raised a Shield, they lose the benefits, as they raise the shield above their head where it's of little use to block attacks. With their hands in the air, each of these frightened creatures can't use reactions or free actions that require their hands, or items held in their hands, until the beginning of their next turn. Regardless of the result, each creature is then temporarily immune to Reach for the Sky for 1 minute.

[Reach for the Stars](/Feats.aspx?ID=3211) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 119

**Prerequisites**
[Black Powder Boost](/Feats.aspx?ID=3166)

</column>

---

The sky's the limit, as long as you've got enough black powder. When you use Black Powder Boost, you can expend additional black powder or ammunition to boost yourself farther. For each dose of black powder or piece of firearm ammunition you spend in addition to your shot, you add another 10 feet to the height or distance of your [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=81), to a maximum of 5 boosts (a +50-foot status bonus). You must be wearing a dose of black powder or piece of ammunition, or have it in hand, to detonate it for a boost.

 You can choose at which points in your Leap you detonate each boost, allowing you to change direction each time. You must then move in a straight line until you boost again or end your Leap.

You channel your necrotic magic through a thrall, expending it in the process. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Reactive Charm](/Feats.aspx?ID=3364) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 121

**Archetype** [Captivator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=125)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Captivator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3358)

**Trigger**
You are the target of a spell or attack.

</column>

---

You're so charming and distracting that when pressed, you can cast a simple enchantment in time to foil an attacker. You cast any of your 1st-level [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61) spells that normally take two actions or fewer to cast. This takes effect before the triggering spell or attack, and if the attacker is affected by your spell, it can make different decisions based on the effects (for instance, if you [_charm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=34) the attacker and it becomes [friendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=18) to you, it can choose a different target than you for its attack or spell). The attacking creature must be in range of your chosen spell, and if your spell requires targets, the attacking creature must be a valid target. Your spell affects only the attacking creature, even if it would normally affect more targets or an area.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=687" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 177

**Prerequisites**
Legendary in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5); [Perfect Distraction](/Feats.aspx?ID=4983)

**Trigger**
You would be hit by an attack or targeted by an effect, or you are within an effect’s area

**Requirements**
You have Perfect Distraction ready to use

</column>

---

You reactively switch with your decoy to foil your foe. You use Perfect Distraction, even if you were observed, as long as you end the movement of your Sneak while concealed or in a location with cover or greater cover. Your decoy is targeted by the attack or effect instead of you. In the case of an area effect, if your Sneak doesn’t move you out of the area, both you and the decoy are targeted by the effect.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Commander" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=855" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=687" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 176

**Trigger**
An adjacent enemy begins to use a reaction

</column>

---

Grabbing a sleeve, swiping with your weapon, or creating another obstruction, you reflexively foil an enemy’s response. If the triggering creature’s level is equal to or lower than yours, you disrupt the triggering reaction. If the triggering creature’s level is higher than yours, you must make an attack roll against its AC. On a success, you disrupt the reaction.

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetypes** [Viking](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=81) (Level 4), [Viking](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=268) (Level 4)

**Trigger**
An enemy hits you with a melee Strike.

</column>

---

You can snap your shield into place just as you would take a blow, avoiding the hit at the last second. You immediately use the [Raise a Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=98) action and gain your shield's bonus to AC. The circumstance bonus from the shield applies to your AC when you're determining the outcome of the triggering attack.

[Reactive Spellshift](/Feats.aspx?ID=9360) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 103

**Archetype** [Spellshifter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=394)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellshifter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9355)

**Trigger**
A creature within 30 feet casts a spell.

**Requirements**
You are holding your conduit.

</column>

---

You can reflexively shift a spell even as it’s being cast. You attempt to Shift the triggering Spell even if you do not meet the other requirements to Shift Spell. On a success, the spellshift applies to the spell’s effects as appropriate for the chosen spellshift. After you choose your spellshift, but before you attempt your [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) check, the caster can voluntarily let their spell be [disrupted](/Rules.aspx?ID=2236). Regardless of the outcome, the caster then becomes immune to your Reactive Spellshift for 10 minutes.

You can read lips of others nearby who you can clearly see. The language read must be one that you know. When you’re at your leisure, you can do this automatically. In encounter mode or when attempting a more difficult feat of lipreading, you’re fascinated and off-guard during each round in which you focus on lip movements, and you must succeed at a Society check (DC determined by the GM) to successfully read someone’s lips.

>
[Read Psychometric Resonance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3776) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=60" />
<trait label="Exploration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=66" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 79

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11)

</column>

---

With a touch, you can read the psychic impressions left on objects by their previous owners. This exploration activity functions similarly to [Detect Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=513) in that you move at half your travel speed or slower while looking for psychometric resonance. You must brush your bare hands over any objects you pass while you do this. This detects objects with significant emotional resonance attached to them, such as the joy from a child's beloved teddy bear, the sorrow from a widower's wedding ring, or the fear from a victim's murder weapon. If you're looking for a particular type of emotional resonance, you can choose to ignore other emotions. If you find an item with that resonance, you can explore that resonance with the following action.

 **Psychometric Assessment** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [exploration](/Traits.aspx?ID=66), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Requirements** Your bare hands are touching an object in which you detected psychometric resonance; **Effect** You spend 1 minute concentrating on the object to get a vision of the face of the person who imbued the item with such emotion in the first place. If the associated emotion is painfully negative, you might take 1d6 psychic damage, as determined by the GM.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 7"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Read Shibboleths](/Feats.aspx?ID=1998) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Linguistic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=101" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 178

**Archetypes** [Linguist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=64), [Venture-Gossip](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=311) (Level 7)

**Prerequisites**
[Linguist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1993); Master in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14)

</column>

---

All communication is filled with slight tells and signals. If you interact with someone for at least 10 minutes, their regional words, pronunciation changes, and nonverbal cues provide you with a minor fact about their social environment, such as their hometown or certain groups they might belong to. If a target of this ability is being deceptive about their social environment, such as a commoner pretending to be a noble, they must attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5), [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14), or appropriate [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) check against your Society DC, providing you a false minor fact consistent with their assumed identity on a success.

 Once you've gleaned one or more true minor facts about a person, you can then incorporate these mannerisms into your speech to present yourself in a way that they find familiar. This grants you a +1 circumstance bonus to your [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) and Deception checks with them.

Once you’ve gleaned one or more true minor facts about a person, you can then incorporate these mannerisms into your speech to present yourself in a way that they find familiar. This grants you a +1 circumstance bonus to your Diplomacy and Deception checks with them.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Lizardfolk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=226" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 47

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Astrology Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) or Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11)

</column>

---

You're incredibly skilled in iruxi astrology, and you can gain useful (if cryptic) hints from the stars' alignment. Once per night, if you can clearly see the stars, you can spend 1 hour reading the heavens to see how they relate to a particular goal, event, or activity that will occur within 1 week. The GM rolls a secret check, either a DC 28 [Astrology Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) check or a DC 32 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) check. On a success, you learn a cryptic clue or piece of advice that could help with the chosen event, and on a critical failure, you learn a misleading cryptic clue or piece of advice.

**Archetype** [Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=175)

**Prerequisites**
able to cast [_animate dead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=666) with a spell slot

</column>

---

You have dedicated your studies to the art of raising and commanding undead. If you're a spontaneous spellcaster with _animate dead_ in your repertoire, it becomes a signature spell in addition to your usual signature spells. If you're a prepared spellcaster with _animate dead_ in your spells known, spellbook, or the like, you can spend 10 minutes contemplating undeath to replace one of the spells you've prepared in your spell slots with an animate dead spell of the same level. In addition, if you're able to target the mostly intact remains of an appropriate type of dead creature when casting _animate dead_, the undead you animate gains a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, AC, saving throws, and skill checks for the duration of _animate dead_.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the reanimator archetype.

<title level="2">Reanimator Dedication leads to...</title>
[Bonds of Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=3489), [Deathly Secrets](/Feats.aspx?ID=3487), [Macabre Virtuoso](/Feats.aspx?ID=3488)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 71

**Archetype** [Cavalier](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=244)

**Prerequisites**
[Cavalier Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6286); Expert in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40)

**Requirements**
You are riding your mount.

</column>

---

You've trained your mount to make an impressive attack and can leverage its presence to terrify your enemies. You  [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400) to order your mount to rear up and make a melee Strike against a creature within its reach. On a successful hit, you can attempt an Intimidation check to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) the target. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to this Intimidation check (+2 if the Strike was a critical hit).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 79

**Archetypes** [Horizon Walker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=63), [Scout](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=73) (Level 4)

**Prerequisites**
[Horizon Walker Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1987) or [Scout Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2047)

**Access**
Members of the Firebrands at the rank of second mark or higher have access to this feat.

**Trigger**
You roll initiative.

</column>

---

Rebellions require an intricate knowledge of one's surroundings—because you might need to escape at any moment. You remember the locations of escape routes, ambush spots, and cover from a scouting expedition or a previous visit to the area. Roll a d20. At any point during the subsequent combat, you can substitute the result of this roll instead of rolling a d20 on one [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) check to [Create a Diversion](/Actions.aspx?ID=45) or on one [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 18"
    pfs=""
>
[Rebellious Existence](/Feats.aspx?ID=7370) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 125

**Archetype** [Broken Chain](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=291)

**Prerequisites**
[Broken Chain Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7357)

</column>

---

You have tied yourself so absolutely to the cause of liberty that your very existence is an act of rebellion. You ignore any [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects without the [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598) trait that would rob you of your agency (for example, on a failed save against [_charm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1463) you would still be able to take hostile actions, and against [_laughing fit_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1583) you would still be able to take reactions but would remain [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92), but on a critical failure against fear you would still be fleeing because it’s a fear effect). Additionally, you are [immune](/Rules.aspx?ID=1609) to effects that would imprison your soul (such as [_seize soul_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1664), or a [final blade](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1094)).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Rebirth in Living Stone](/Feats.aspx?ID=4234) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=127" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 27

</column>

---

Rock overflows from within you to consume your form before cracking open to reveal your body transformed into living stone. You gain 40 temporary Hit Points. You're immune to critical hits and precision damage. You can't be [pushed, pulled](/Rules.aspx?ID=451), or tripped while you're standing on earth or stone. Your earth [Elemental Blasts](/Actions.aspx?ID=2125) deal an additional 1d10 damage of their normal type. These benefits last until the end of your next turn, but you can Sustain them up to 1 minute. After you gain temporary Hit Points from this impulse, you can't do so again for 10 minutes.

---
**Level (20th)** You gain 50 temporary Hit Points.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Rebounding Assault](/Feats.aspx?ID=3186) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 115

**Requirements**
You're wielding a loaded firearm or loaded crossbow in one hand and a bludgeoning or slashing melee weapon in the other.

</column>

---

You hurl your melee weapon at an opponent, then fire a bullet into the weapon's hilt, making it bounce back to your grasp. Make a thrown ranged Strike with the melee weapon, then a ranged Strike with your firearm. Both Strikes use your current multiple attack penalty and this counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty. If the melee weapon doesn't already have the [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=711) trait, it gains the thrown 10 feet trait during a Rebounding Assault.

If both attacks are successful, the bolt or bullet hits the thrown melee weapon instead of your target, adding its force into one attack. Combine the damage from both Strikes, using the thrown weapon's damage type, and add an additional 1d6 precision damage. The impact sends the melee weapon rebounding off the target and back to your hand.

 In any circumstance other than both attacks hitting, carry out the individual Strikes normally. The thrown weapon doesn't rebound and remains in the target's space as normal for thrown weapons.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs=""
>
[Receive Prayers](/Feats.aspx?ID=7395) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 132

**Archetype** [Godling](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=293)

**Prerequisites**
[Godling Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7392)

</column>

---

You open your senses so the prayers of mortals can better reach your ears. You gain a +1 status bonus to checks to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302), but only when attempting to ascertain hopes, prayers, wishes, and other strongly held desires of the target. You gain an even greater sense of your hierophant's prayers, which grants you a constant [_status_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1690) as a constant [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spell targeting your hierophant. The spell has unlimited duration and functions at any range, included across planar boundaries, and [counteracting](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) the spell merely suppresses it until your next [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575), though it automatically ends if the creature stops being your hierophant. 

You gain the ability to cast [_breath of life_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1456) once per day as a 5th-rank divine innate spell. You can cast this spell only on your hierophant, and the spell has unlimited range (your status spell typically alerting to you to when your hierophant would die).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=953" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 19

**Prerequisites**
[twofold tine hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=15)

**Requirements**
You’re wielding two melee weapons, each in a different hand.

</column>

---

The clash of steel fuels your magic, preparing you to unleash another magic-infused assault. Make one [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) with each of your weapons, then recharge your [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755) (regardless of whether the Strikes hit). Your multiple attack penalty increases after each Strike as normal. If the second Strike targets a creature you haven’t attacked yet this turn, its multiple attack penalty is –4 if it’s your second attack this turn (–3 if you’re using an [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526) weapon) or –8 if it’s your third or further Strike (–6 with an agile weapon).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 140

**Archetype** [Wildspell](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=295)

**Prerequisites**
[Wildspell Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7418)

</column>

---

You can break your spells down into raw magical potential and transfer it to an ally. Expend one prepared spell, spell slot, or [Focus](/Rules.aspx?ID=285) Point, and choose an adjacent ally or an ally within your _spellsurge_ aura. If you expended a spell or spell slot, the ally regains one expended spell or spell slot with a rank equal to or lower than the spell or spell slot you expended. If you expended a Focus Point, the ally regains a Focus Point. This feat can’t grant more spell slots or Focus Points than the target can normally possess. You can’t target yourself with this ability. Only one spell, spell slot, or Focus Point can be transferred with each use of this ability.

<traits>

<trait label="Rage" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=135" />

Your blood boils when you take a beating, and you throw caution to the wind to finish the fight. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to attack rolls, a –2 penalty to AC, and a –1 penalty to saves. These bonuses and penalties last until your Rage ends or until you are above half Hit Points, whichever comes first.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 17"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Reckless Abandon (Goblin)](/Feats.aspx?ID=1429) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=76" />
<trait label="Goblin" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=81" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 45

**Frequency**
once per day

</column>

---

Despite a lifetime filled with questionable decisions, you've managed to survive, as though you have uncanny luck that lets you avoid the consequences of your own actions. For the remainder of your turn, if you roll a failure or critical failure on a saving throw against a harmful effect, you get a success instead. Further, enemies and hazards that would damage you this turn roll the minimum possible damage.

 These benefits apply only to harmful effects incurred entirely during your turn in which you activate Reckless Abandon, such as running through a [_prismatic wall_](/Spells.aspx?ID=234). Persistent damage and conditions that were applied prior to your turn proceed normally, and as soon as your turn ends you are subject to the full consequences of any dangers still threatening you.

[Reclaimant Plea](/Feats.aspx?ID=3593) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 77

**Archetype** [Knight Reclaimant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=28)

**Prerequisites**
[Knight Reclaimant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1097); ability to cast divine spells

</column>

---

You call on the power of the Crimson Oath to gain magical aid. Choose one of the following spells: [_air walk_](/Spells.aspx?ID=6), [_dimensional anchor_](/Spells.aspx?ID=70), [_freedom of movement_](/Spells.aspx?ID=128), [_invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=164), [_remove curse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=250), [_searing light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=269). You can Cast that Spell once per day as a 4th-level divine innate spell. At 14th level, the spell heightens to 5th level, and at 16th level, the spell heightens to 6th level. If you anger the mysterious source of the Crimson Oath's power, you lose the ability to cast the spell until you atone.

**Special** You can select this feat a second time at 14th level, gaining a second spell from the list above, [_death ward_](/Spells.aspx?ID=64), or [_flame strike_](/Spells.aspx?ID=120), which you can cast once per day; you also become an expert in divine spell DCs and divine spell attack rolls. You can select this feat a third time at 18th level, gaining either a third spell from the list above, _death ward_, _flame strike_, or [_sunburst_](/Spells.aspx?ID=326), which you can cast once per day; additionally, all three spells from this feat heighten to 7th level, and you become a master of divine spell attacks and spell DCs.

<title level="2">Reclaimant Plea leads to...</title>
[May Death Itself Reconsider](/Feats.aspx?ID=7749)

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 261 _[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The DC to Recognize an Uncommon or Rare spell should be the normal DC +2 or +5 based on rarity and spell level._ **Prerequisites** Trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) **Trigger** A creature within line of sight casts a spell that you don’t have prepared or in your spell repertoire, or a trap or similar object casts such a spell. You must be aware of the casting. --- If you are trained in the appropriate skill for the spell’s tradition and it’s a common spell of 2nd rank or lower, you automatically identify it (you still roll to attempt to get a critical success, but can’t get a worse result than success). The highest rank of spell you automatically identify increases to 4 if you’re an expert, 6 if you’re a master, and 10 if you’re legendary. The GM rolls a secret Arcana, Nature, Occultism, or Religion check, whichever corresponds to the tradition of the spell being cast. If you’re not trained in the skill, you can’t get a result better than failure. **Critical Success** You correctly recognize the spell and gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your saving throw or your AC against it.
**Success** You correctly recognize the spell.
**Failure** You fail to recognize the spell.
**Critical Failure** You misidentify the spell as another spell entirely, of the GM’s choice. Recognize Spell leads to... [Quick Recognition](/Feats.aspx?ID=5197)

    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Reconstruct the Scene](/Feats.aspx?ID=1478) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=318" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=139" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 65

</column>

---

You spend 1 minute surveying a small location (such as a single room) to get an impression of events that occurred there in the last day. This involves moving about the area and studying footprints, the placement of objects, spilled drinks or blood, and so forth. You get an indistinct mental impression of significant events that happened there. This gives you clues and details of the past, including the overall events and their time frame, but it's not a perfect record. This also isn't enough to identify who was involved in these events if you weren't already aware the person was there. As determined by the GM, you also pick out various seemingly small details that could serve as important clues, like a memorable weapon someone used for a murder or the type of cloak someone wore when passing through.

    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Reconstruct The Scene](/Feats.aspx?ID=4984) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=818" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=687" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 177, [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 113

</column>

---

You spend 1 minute surveying a small location (such as a single room) to get an impression of events that occurred there in the last day. This involves moving about the area and studying footprints, spilled drinks or blood, and so forth. You get an indistinct mental impression of significant events that happened there. This gives you clues and details of the past, including the overall events and their time frame, but it’s not a perfect record. This also isn’t enough to identify who was involved in these events if you weren’t already aware the person was there. As determined by the GM, you also pick out various seemingly small details that could serve as important clues, like a memorable weapon someone used for a murder or the type of cloak someone wore when passing through.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Metamagic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=107" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 48

**Archetype** [Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134)

**Requirements**
An enemy's action disrupted your attempts to Cast a Spell since the beginning of your last turn.

</column>

---

You recover the energy of a recently disrupted spell, allowing you to cast it again as long as you do so immediately before the energy dissipates. You regain the use of a spell that was disrupted since the beginning of your last turn, but you must immediately Cast the Spell again with your next action or else you lose the spell; as normal for metamagic, this must be on the same turn that you use Recover Spell. You can change the area, targets, and other variables, including the number of actions used to Cast the Spell if the spell allows, such as when casting [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=148) or [_magic missile_](/Spells.aspx?ID=180).

[Red Herring](/Feats.aspx?ID=1453) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=318" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 61

</column>

---

You have a keen sense for avoiding spurious lines of inquiry. When you Pursue a Lead, the GM tells you if the lead you chose is inconsequential. For example, if you found a splatter of gray mud on the wall, thought it was suspicious, and Pursued it as a Lead, the GM would tell you if there was no greater mystery related to it. When the GM tells you a lead is inconsequential, you can decline to Pursue the Lead, keeping any leads you were already pursuing. You still can't use Pursue a Lead again for 10 minutes, as normal.

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 35 **Usage** imbued into a weapon ikon --- By channeling your divinity into a creature along with a strike, you can disrupt their ability to recover. The imbued ikon gains the following ability. **Immanence** When you successfully damage an enemy with the ikon, a marking appears around the wound, painted in the red of mortal blood and the gold of divine ichor. When the target would regain Hit Points, such as from a [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623) effect or an ability like [fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=62) or [regeneration](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=72), it must attempt a Will save against your class DC to determine the effects, and then the marking fades. The marking otherwise fades after 1 minute. **Success** The creature regains the full number of Hit Points that would be healed.
**Failure** The creature regains only half the number of Hit Points as the contradictory energies swirl within it.
**Critical Failure** The creature doesn’t regain any Hit Points.

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 103 **Archetype** [Spellshifter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=394) **Prerequisites** [Spellshifter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9355) --- You can alter the flow of magic around you, moving a spell effect from one target to another. You gain the Redirect Magic spellshift. **Spellshift—Redirect Magic** Through sheer force of will, you can direct a spell’s energies away from its caster’s intended target. **Critical Success** You change a single target of the spell to another viable target within 30 feet of you (even if it would be outside of the spell’s normal range). You can’t use this spellshift to affect a creature twice with the same spell. If the spell had an initial saving throw, the new target must attempt it, possibly achieving a different result than the original target of the spell. The DC for the spell becomes your [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) DC instead of the original caster’s spell DC.
**Success** As critical success, but if the target succeeds at any required saving throw, they are unaffected, and the spell does not change targets.

>
[Redirect Teleportation](/Feats.aspx?ID=9391) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=156" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 109

**Trigger**
A creature teleports into a space within 60 feet of you.

</column>

---

You’re able to intercept a teleportation effect and change where a creature appears. You expend a prepared spell that has the [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) trait. You lose your spell slot as if you had cast the triggering spell. You then attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) the triggering spell. The counteract rank for this effect is equal to the rank of the expended spell. If you succeed on your counteract check, you don’t [disrupt](/Rules.aspx?ID=2236) the spell. Instead, you choose an unoccupied space within 60 feet of you for the creature to teleport into. You can’t choose a space that is obviously harmful (such as into a [_wall of fire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1748) or [hazardous terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2587)) or would cause the target to fall.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Reflecting Riposte](/Feats.aspx?ID=1247) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=71" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #156: The Apocalypse Prophet](/Sources.aspx?ID=36) pg. 72

**Prerequisites**
[Dueling Riposte](/Feats.aspx?ID=389), [Mirror Shield](/Feats.aspx?ID=404), or [Twin Riposte](/Feats.aspx?ID=523)

**Trigger**
An opponent casts a spell and you critically succeed at a saving throw against it.

**Requirements**
You have a shield raised or are benefiting from [Dueling Parry](/Feats.aspx?ID=367) or [Twin Parry](/Feats.aspx?ID=377).

</column>

---

You attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the triggering spell using powerful magical techniques observed in the Kortos Mounts. Use your attack roll modifier with your shield or parrying weapon for your counteract check. If you counteract the spell, it is reflected upon the caster. If the spell targeted individual creatures, it targets the caster only. If the spell targeted an area centered on a point, the new area is centered on the caster. If the spell was a cone or line, the cone or line emanates from you toward the caster. If the spell has a save DC, it uses your class DC, and if it requires a spell attack roll, use the same attack roll modifier as the counteract check.

**Source** [Pathfinder #156: The Apocalypse Prophet](/Sources.aspx?ID=36) pg. 72

**Related Feats**: [Annihilating Swing](/Feats.aspx?ID=1240), [Astonishing Explosion](/Feats.aspx?ID=1241), [Banishing Blow](/Feats.aspx?ID=1242), [Denier of Destruction](/Feats.aspx?ID=1243), [Endurance of the Rooted Tree](/Feats.aspx?ID=1244), [Mimic Protections](/Feats.aspx?ID=1245), [Reclaim Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=1246), [Ringmaster's Introduction](/Feats.aspx?ID=1248), [Steal Essence](/Feats.aspx?ID=1249), [Tenacious Blood Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=1250), [Verdant Presence](/Feats.aspx?ID=1251)

---

You've formed a connection with a small hand mirror, allowing you to use it as an extradimensional storage space. You can store one item of light Bulk in your mirror at a time. Storing or retrieving an item requires an Interact action and any creature can do so. While an item is stored within the mirror, the mirror reflects the item's image. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks to [Conceal an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=61) unless someone checks the mirror's reflection.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Reflective Ripple Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=2980) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=112" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=152" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 202

**Requirements**
You're unarmored.

</column>

---

You enter a stance of fluid grace as small amounts of water flow with your movements and attacks. You can make flowing wave attacks that deal 1d6 bludgeoning damage. They are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group and have the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [disarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=175), [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=196), [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199), and [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165) traits.

 While in Reflective Ripple Stance, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41), [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39), or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40), and you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Reflex DC to avoid being Disarmed and Tripped.

**Special** This feat gains your choice of either the [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48) or [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120) trait, matching your ki spell tradition if possible.

<title level="2">Reflective Ripple Stance leads to...</title>
[Rippling Spin](/Feats.aspx?ID=2983), [Wave Spiral](/Feats.aspx?ID=2985)

An item falls within your reach or an attacker fails an attack roll to hit you or a creature within your reach with a thrown weapon.

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 101 **Archetype** [Wandering Chef](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=277) **Prerequisites** [Morning Side Dishes](/Feats.aspx?ID=7054) --- You can create dishes that reflect the food sources endemic to your environment and medicinal food techniques utilizing the cycle of the five elements. When you create alchemical food from Morning Side Dishes during your daily preparations, you can add one elemental benefit of your choice to each of the items. This benefit comes in addition to any other effect of consuming the item. Each element has an immediate benefit and a +3 item bonus to certain saves that lasts for 1 hour after the food is consumed. The item bonus increases to +4 if the alchemical item is 18th level or higher.
  • **Wood** Remove one source of [persistent bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86). For 1 hour, gain a +3 item bonus to saves against [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578) and [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) effects.
  • **Fire** Reduce the [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) condition by 1. For 1 hour, gain a +3 item bonus to saves against being [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) or [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76)
  • **Earth** Reduce the [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) condition by 1. For 1 hour, gain a +3 item bonus to saves against being [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71).
  • **Metal** Reduce the [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) condition by 1. For 1 hour, gain a +3 item bonus to saves against being stupefied.
  • **Water** Reduce the frightened condition by 2. For 1 hour, gain a +3 item bonus to saves against [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66) or drained.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 78

**Archetype** [Heroic Scion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=339)

**Prerequisites**
[Heroic Scion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8151); [familiar](/Rules.aspx?ID=2121) or [nimble](/Companions.aspx?Type=Advancement&amp;ID=7) or [savage](/Companions.aspx?Type=Advancement&amp;ID=8) animal companion

</column>

---

You’re not alone in having a legendary past life—so too does your companion. This previous life might be the return of an animal companion or familiar a previous PC of yours had that perished, or it could be the reincarnation of an entirely different legendary creature. It could even be the returning spirit of a close friend or ally who stood by your side. If you have an animal companion, it gains one specialization of your choice. If you have a familiar, it gains two additional familiar abilities. If your fated companion is slain, you can replace it at no cost when you perform your daily preparations.

---

Your body is designed to be particularly resilient. Your chassis is made from reinforced armor plating that grants a +3 item bonus to AC with a Dexterity cap of +1. If you are at least 5th level, the item bonus increases to +4 and at 10th level it increases to +5. You can never wear other armor or remove your chassis; however, you still don’t become fatigued from sleeping. Finally, you can etch armor runes onto your chassis. Your chassis is medium armor in the plate group for abilities and for etching runes.

**Enhancement** Your chassis becomes difficult to overcome. You gain the Chassis Deflection reaction.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 37 **Frequency** once per hour **Prerequisites** [whose cry is thunder](/Epithets.aspx?ID=12) or [dancer in the seasons](/Epithets.aspx?ID=8) --- You hold your arms out, and the fury of the seasons comes to your jubilant embrace. A storm spirals out from you, dealing 5d8 damage (see below) to each creature in a 30-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387), with a basic Reflex save against your class DC. At 10th level and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d8. The emanation is quartered into four non-overlapping cones, each of a different season, which must be arranged clockwise from spring, to summer, to fall, to winter. Each cone has different traits, damage type, and a different effect to a creature that critically fails its saving throw; a creature large enough to be in multiple seasons can choose which it is affected by.
• **Spring** (electricity) Spring lightning deals electricity damage. Creatures who critically fail are left numb, becoming clumsy 2 until the end of their next turn.
• **Summer** (water) A summer monsoon deals bludgeoning damage. Creatures who critically fail are knocked prone by hurricane winds.
• **Fall** (emotion, mental, wood) Falling leaves deal slashing damage. Creatures who critically fail are gripped by melancholy, becoming off-guard until the end of their next turn.
• **Winter** (cold) A blizzard deals cold damage. Creatures who critically fail are stupefied 2 until the end of their next turn as the cold numbs their senses.

fields.text: Feat 8 Rejoice in Solstice Storm Two Actions Concentrate Divine Exemplar Manipulate Source War of Immortals pg. 37 Frequency once per hour Prerequisites whose cry is thunder or dancer in the seasons You hold your arms out, and the fury of the seasons comes to your jubilant embrace. A storm spirals out from you, dealing 5d8 damage (see below) to each creature in a 30-foot emanation, with a basic Reflex save against your class DC. At 10th level and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d8. The emanation is quartered into four non-overlapping cones, each of a different season, which must be arranged clockwise from spring, to summer, to fall, to winter. Each cone has different traits, damage type, and a different effect to a creature that critically fails its saving throw; a creature large enough to be in multiple seasons can choose which it is affected by. • Spring (electricity) Spring lightning deals electricity damage. Creatures who critically fail are left numb, becoming clumsy 2 until the end of their next turn. • Summer (water) A summer monsoon deals bludgeoning damage. Creatures who critically fail are knocked prone by hurricane winds. • Fall (emotion, mental, wood) Falling leaves deal slashing damage. Creatures who critically fail are gripped by melancholy, becoming off-guard until the end of their next turn. • Winter (cold) A blizzard deals cold damage. Creatures who critically fail are stupefied 2 until the end of their next turn as the cold numbs their senses.

You rejuvenate your spirit by taking your rest where Mother Earth embraces Father Moon. When you rest outdoors, you can choose one of the following benefits, which lasts until your next sleep cycle and can’t be changed.

**Mother Earth’s Care** After 8 hours of sleep, you regain additional Hit Points equal to your Constitution modifier plus your level.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Skeleton" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=236" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 56

</column>

---

You tie yourself to the [Material Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=1) by implanting a piece of your consciousness into a weapon, piece of armor, or other item that's precious to you. As long as this object is intact, even if your body is destroyed, you can be restored to the exact state you were in the last time you made daily preparations with this object in your possession. The soulbound object can be used as a special focus for [_raise dead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=243), [_resurrect_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=20), or similar magic. This warps the spell to bring you back in your skeletal undead state rather than bringing you back to life. [Pharasma](/Deities.aspx?ID=14) can't prevent you from returning when the spell is modified in this way.

 When you return, you permanently lose a memory that was precious to you, in addition to any other side effects of the spell that brought you back. Your soulbound object becomes inert until you spend 1 week of downtime to anchor yourself to it again, further fragmenting your mind.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=606" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 123

**Archetype** [Broken Chain](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=291)

**Prerequisites**
[Broken Chain Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7357)

**Requirements**
An enemy has you [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90).

</column>

---

Your retribution against one who would detain you is swift and dangerous. Make a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) against the creature who has you [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90). You can still make this attack even if you are restrained, though not if you are wielding a two-handed weapon. Unless your Strike is a critical failure, you can then attempt a check to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296). If the creature who has you grabbed or restrained is the target of your [Ultimatum of Liberation](/Actions.aspx?ID=2993), you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to this check. Both the Strike and the Escape count toward your multiple attack penalty, but it doesn’t increase until you’ve made both rolls.

Many people report seeing a bright light before their death. You’re one of these people, and at rare intervals when hope seems dim, the light exudes outward from your soul. You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius (and dim light for another 30 feet beyond that) until the end of your next turn. Enemy creatures in the area that rely on sight must attempt a Fortitude save equal to your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. Critical Success The creature is unaffected. Success The creature is dazzled for 1 round. Failure The creature is blinded for 1 round and dazzled for 1 minute. Critical Failure The creature is blinded for 2 rounds and dazzled for 1 minute.

<title

    right="Feat 14"

>
[Reliable Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=8141) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 73

**Archetype** [Avenging Runelord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=338)

**Prerequisites**
[Avenging Runelord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8139)

</column>

---

Magic stored in written form or within wands is more reliable in your capable hands. Whenever you overcharge a wand, reduce the DC of the flat check to avoid destroying the wand by 4. It still gains the broken condition on a success.

When you [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) from a scroll you can spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323) as a free action. The spell is cast at mythic proficiency. Once you cast the spell using this ability, attempt a DC 11 flat check. If this check is successful, the scroll is not destroyed, and instead glows with light equivalent to that of a candle for 10 minutes. You can Cast a Spell from this scroll again, but if you do so you cannot enhance it in any way (such as by using this feat), and the scroll is destroyed. If not used before the end of the 10 minutes, the scroll is destroyed.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Relinquish Control](/Feats.aspx?ID=7122) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Animist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=836" />
<trait label="Apparition" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=837" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 22

**Trigger**
Your turn begins.

</column>

---

Your apparition takes over and shields you from outside influence. Until the start of your next turn, you gain a +4 status bonus on saves against spells and effects that give you the [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) condition or attempt to influence your actions (such as [_charm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1463), [_command_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1470), or a [nosoi’s](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3147) haunting melody). However, the only actions you can take are to [Recall Knowledge](/Rules.aspx?ID=2638), [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304), [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306), [Cast an apparition Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734), Cast a vessel Spell, [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) a vessel spell, or use an action that has the [apparition](/Traits.aspx?ID=837) trait. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus on all Recall Knowledge checks made using Lore skills granted by your attuned apparitions.

**Special** This feat requires a particularly strong bond with a specific apparition to learn. Choose one apparition you have access to; once you learn this feat, you must always choose that apparition as one of the apparitions you attune to each day.

<title level="2">Relinquish Control leads to...</title>
[Instinctive Maneuvers](/Feats.aspx?ID=7136)

[Reloading Trick](/Feats.aspx?ID=2685) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #165: Eyes of Empty Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=81) pg. 77

**Archetype** [Drow Shootist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=90)

**Frequency**
once per round

**Prerequisites**
[Drow Shootist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2683)

**Requirements**
You're holding an unloaded hand crossbow.

</column>

---

You can fire off a single shot even when unprepared. You Interact to reload your [hand crossbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=69) and [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=89) with it.

**Special** If you have the [Repeating Hand Crossbow Training](/Feats.aspx?ID=2684) feat, you can use this feat with a [repeating hand crossbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=160) to load either a bolt or a magazine, but the speed means you can fire only one bolt, then the magazine jams. You must spend a 3-action Interact activity to remove the jammed magazine and clear it before it can be used again.

    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Remake the World](/Feats.aspx?ID=7194) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
<trait label="Exemplar" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=839" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 43

**Prerequisites**
[Strike Rivers, Seize Winds](/Feats.aspx?ID=7187)

</column>

---

For the briefest of moments, you can reach into the realm of true gods, gaining the power to shape reality to your will. Once per day, you can create the effects of a [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spell of 8th level or lower. The spell must be common or one to which you otherwise have access, and it costs as many actions as it would typically take to cast. Use your class DC in place of any necessary spell DC and your class DC –10 in place of any necessary counteract modifier or spell attack modifier. Because you are creating these effects with your godly might rather than Casting a Spell, they can’t be dispelled or counteracted, like Strike Rivers, Seize Winds.

fields.text: Feat 20 Remake the World Divine Exemplar Source War of Immortals pg. 43 Prerequisites Strike Rivers, Seize Winds For the briefest of moments, you can reach into the realm of true gods, gaining the power to shape reality to your will. Once per day, you can create the effects of a divine spell of 8th level or lower. The spell must be common or one to which you otherwise have access, and it costs as many actions as it would typically take to cast. Use your class DC in place of any necessary spell DC and your class DC –10 in place of any necessary counteract modifier or spell attack modifier. Because you are creating these effects with your godly might rather than Casting a Spell, they can’t be dispelled or counteracted, like Strike Rivers, Seize Winds.

<traits>
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=541" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Broken Chain](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=291)

**Prerequisites**
[Broken Chain Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7357)

</column>

---

You peer into the eyes of a target of your [Ultimatum of Liberation](/Actions.aspx?ID=2993), as you say aloud the names of their victims, searing them into the oppressor’s mind, cursing them to feel their victims’ pain. The target takes 12d6 mental damage ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Will save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher). If the target fails or critically fails this check, they also take 2d6 [persistent mental damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86). For the next hour, when the target stops taking this persistent damage, you or one of your allies can mention a victim’s name as a single action to the target, forcing them to succeed at another Will save or begin taking the persistent damage again. This is a [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=566) effect. Once you use Remember Their Names on a target, the target is immune to it for 24 hours.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Amp" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=425" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Psychic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=430" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 27

</column>

---

Your spell reaches into the mind of a creature and removes you from it. The amped cantrip must be one that has one or more targets and must either require a spell attack roll or have a saving throw. Use this amp in place of the psi cantrip's normal amp entry.

---
**Amp** Choose one target of the spell or one creature in its area. If that enemy fails its save or the spell hits it, you become [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) by that creature, disappearing from its senses for 1 minute or until you use a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300). This is similar to being [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26), but effects like [_see invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=271) don't reveal you—you're affecting the target's mind, not its vision. [_True seeing_](/Spells.aspx?ID=344) can still see through this illusion if the [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check succeeds.

You become trained in the [repeating hand crossbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=160) and gain access to repeating hand crossbows and [shootist bandoliers](/Equipment.aspx?ID=937). Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in a given weapon or weapons, you also gain that proficiency in the repeating hand crossbow. If you're at least an expert in a repeating hand crossbow you're using, you gain access to its critical specialization effect. You can perform the [Shootist's Draw](/Feats.aspx?ID=2683) action with repeating hand crossbows.

**Special** If you have the [Running Reload](/Feats.aspx?ID=504) feat, you can reload a repeating hand crossbow magazine on the move. You can use Running Reload as a 3-action activity to reload a magazine into a repeating hand crossbow after you [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=88), [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=87), or [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63), or as a 2-action activity if you use a magazine from a shootist bandolier.

Your Calling demands that you defy danger and injury to yourself or those who rely on you while allowing you to respond to the originators of such aggression with ferocious and unrivaled fury. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320); you gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) to the triggering attack equal to your level. If you [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) the enemy that made the attack before the end of your next turn, you can make that Strike at mythic proficiency. This benefit applies only to the first Strike you make against that enemy.

Your stoicism and courage seem to drive off darkness and shadow. For 1 minute, you suppress magical [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=569) effects of a rank equal to or lower than half your level rounded up within a 10-foot emanation. This doesn't provide light, but merely restores the area to its natural illumination level. You can Dismiss this aura.

 If your horse is at least a mature animal companion, you can use Repel Darkness to cause the aura to emanate from your horse instead of you, as long as your horse is within 100 feet.

<traits>

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 205

</column>

---

You’ve discovered how to reuse some of your spell slots over and over. You can spend 10 minutes to prepare a spell that you already cast today, regaining access to that spell slot. The spell must be of 4th rank or lower and can’t have a duration. You can reprepare a spell in this way even if you’ve already reprepared that spell previously in the same day.

Any shield you wield gains the [shove](/Traits.aspx?ID=193) trait. When you [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) using a shield and Stride as part of that action, you can move an additional 5 feet to either side of the creature you Shoved. In addition, if you are in the [Everstand Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=1087) and successfully Shove a creature using a shield that you wield two-handed, you can increase the distance of your Shove to 10 feet.

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 68

The following feats represent benefits of training from the Iomedars (Kalabrynne for knight vigilant, Clarethe for knight reclaimant, either for Lastwall sentry).

---

When you enter your Arcane Cascade, you disperse the magical reinforcement to nearby allies. You grant the extra damage of Arcane Cascade in an aura affecting all allies in a 5-foot emanation. ---

The magical reinforcement from your [Arcane Cascade](/Actions.aspx?ID=756) extends to nearby allies. While you’re in Arcane Cascade stance, you grant its extra damage and resistance in an aura affecting all allies in a 5-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). This uses only the base values of your stance; it doesn’t use any increase you get from bonuses, the [laughing shadow hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=2), or the like. As normal for duplicate effects, multiple Arcane Cascades affecting the same creature aren’t cumulative.

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Restorative Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=4659) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cleric" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=554" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 116

**Requirements**
You have a [harm](/Spells.aspx?ID=1552) or [heal](/Spells.aspx?ID=1554) spell you can cast

</column>

---

You balance both sides of the scales, restoring yourself while striking a foe. Cast a 1-action _harm_ or _heal_ spell to heal yourself, expending the spell normally. It loses the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) trait when cast this way. Then make a melee Strike. If you make this Strike with your deity's favored weapon, you gain a +1 status bonus to the attack roll.

If the Strike hits, you can target a second willing creature to heal the same amount from the spell. This creature can be outside of the spell's range, provided it's adjacent to the enemy you hit.

---

Your body can process an alternative to your venom that heals wounds. You can use your Envenom action to produce a blood restorative instead of vishkanyan venom. You can make a blood restorative at most once per 10 minutes, even if your Envenom action can be used more frequently. You or an adjacent creature can Interact to consume the restorative to regain 3d6 Hit Points. This is a [positive](/Traits.aspx?ID=128) [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=89) effect. A restorative spoils at the start of your next turn.

 When you reach 15th level, the restorative restores 5d6 Hit Points instead.

---

When you absorb a spell using the [Absorb Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=1138) reaction, you utilize secret, techniques that allow you to retain the power and knowledge necessary to cast the spell repeatedly—potentially for a greater period of time. If you're a spontaneous caster, you can cast the triggering spell up to three times instead of once. If you're a prepared spellcaster, you can replace up to three of your prepared spells of the same level with the absorbed spell instead of one. Either way, you can choose to retain the absorbed spell for the next hour instead of the next 10 minutes; if you choose to extend the absorption to an hour, you can't use Absorb Spell again until one hour after the spell is absorbed.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Guardian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=859" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 44

</column>

---

When an ally is in danger, you can hustle to reach them and punish the foe threatening them. Stride up to your Speed. You must end this movement adjacent to an ally who is within an enemy's reach. Then, you [push](/Rules.aspx?ID=2364) your ally up to 5 feet (as normal for forced movement, this movement doesn't trigger reactions) and make a melee Strike against an enemy within your reach. If your ally was in that enemy's reach and your push moved them out of it, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your attack roll.

</title>

<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=7" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 84

**Frequency**
You're holding  holy water  or a bomb that deals positive damage in one of your hands.

**Access**
Knights of Lastwall have access to this feat.

**Trigger**
You would take damage from an adjacent creature's Strike.

</column>

---

You twist your hand in front of the blow, ensuring the enemy's attack shatters the required _holy water_ or bomb. The creature takes the on-hit and [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150) damage from the _holy water_ or required bomb, not counting any additional effects you would add or apply when you throw the bomb, such as weapon specialization or [Calculated Splash](/Feats.aspx?ID=99). You're splashed by the _holy water_ or required bomb, although since positive damage harms only [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) and creatures with [negative healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=42), it's unlikely you will take damage.

If you wield this symbol in one hand when you spend an extra action while casting banishment on a devil, you don't need to pay the extra cost to give that creature a –2 circumstance penalty to its save.

</title>

<traits>

You adapt a creature to living and moving in water. Target a willing creature within 30 feet. In addition, its attacks ignore the effects water normally has on bludgeoning and slashing attacks. If you use Return to the Sea again, any existing one ends.

---

    right="Feat 17"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Return to the Seed](/Feats.aspx?ID=6860) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Leshy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=639" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 43

</column>

---

Once per month, when you die, you can instead choose to fade away. Your corpse is swallowed by the earth, leaving behind only a seed. This seed is very fragile with an AC of 10 and only 1 Hit Point. Another creature can spend 1 minute to plant the seed in a safe space and water it. If so cared for, the next morning a tree grows from it with a single large fruit or flower bud that splits open to reveal you, alive and returned to maximum Hit Points.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Return Unto Runes](/Feats.aspx?ID=9212) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Runesmith" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=952" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 53

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Trigger**
An enemy targets you with a spell attack or other magical attack against your AC.

</column>

---

You attempt to deconstruct an incoming spell into its individual magical components, storing them temporarily as a rune. You gain a +4 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If the attack misses, the spell becomes sealed in a rune, which floats around you. Until the end of your next turn, you can [Trace this Rune](/Actions.aspx?ID=4264) onto a creature as normal. This rune doesn’t have an effect until it’s invoked.

When the rune is invoked, the rune-bearer is affected by the spell or magical attack captured in the rune. Make a check, using your class DC – 10 as the modifier against the rune‑bearer’s AC to determine the effects.

You have mastered the technique of arcing a projectile so that it returns to your hand after being thrown, though this requires a moment to precisely calculate the trajectory and possible ricochets.
