</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Tiefling" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=258" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 32

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Beastbrood](/Feats.aspx?ID=2449)

**Requirements**
You're [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) to at least one enemy.

</column>

---

While hidden, you manifest a version of your animalistic nature. You create an illusion of a Large or smaller creature within 60 feet of your location with the effects of the [_illusory creature_](/Spells.aspx?ID=158) spell.  The creature shares your animalistic beastbrood features. Unlike most actions taken while hidden, using Reveal Hidden Self and Sustaining the Spell don't automatically end your hidden condition. Use the higher of your class DC or spell DC against attempts to disbelieve the illusion. If a creature observes you, it automatically disbelieves the illusion, and if you're no longer hidden to at least one enemy, the effect ends.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 15"

>
[Reveal Machinations](/Feats.aspx?ID=924) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #147: Tomorrow Must Burn](/Sources.aspx?ID=8) pg. 73

**Prerequisites**
Legendary in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5)

</column>

---

You reveal that you played a minor but recurring role in another humanoid’s life—or at least convince them that’s the case. Attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) check against the target’s Will DC. On a success, the revelation makes them [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) 2, and on a critical success they are frightened 3. In addition, you gain information about the subject as though you had attempted to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about them using an appropriate skill and received the same result on your roll. You can’t use this ability against the same humanoid again until 1 day has passed and you’ve also successfully disguised yourself as a different person.

**Special** At the GM’s discretion, this feat can be used against non-humanoids if they have regular contact with humanoids or you are able to disguise yourself as a member of the target’s ancestry or type of creature.

If the PCs earn Mialari Docur's trust and prove their worth by defeating the Scarlet Triad, she rewards them by granting them access to several feats and spells she and her students have developed over the years.

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 246 **Prerequisites** trained in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) and at least one of [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), [Occult](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), and [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) --- You attempt to get a creature to do as you wish by threatening them with your knowledge of their true name. You must know and speak the creature's true name and say what you want the creature to do. Attempt an Intimidation check against the target's Will DC. **Critical Success** The target does as you say out of a sense of self-preservation, and will not harm itself in any way. It becomes [unfriendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=40) (if it wasn't already unfriendly or hostile) but continues to comply for up to 1 day. The target is too scared of you to retaliate or flee, certain you would find them wherever they might go.
**Success** As critical success, but once the target becomes unfriendly, they avoid you and might act against you in an indirect manner, such as alerting your enemies to your location.
**Failure** The target refuses to comply and typically flees your presence to avoid your further use of their true name. If they were not already unfriendly or [hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=23), they become unfriendly. They avoid you in the future and are likely to take indirect action against you.
**Critical Failure** The target refuses to comply and becomes hostile, if it wasn't already. If they perceive you as weak, they might attack you; otherwise, they likely flee to avoid your further use of their true name.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Revealing Stab](/Feats.aspx?ID=384) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=71" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 148

**Requirements**
You are wielding a melee weapon that deals piercing damage.

</column>

---

You drive your piercing weapon into an imperceptible foe, revealing its location to your allies. Make a Strike with the required melee weapon. You don't have to attempt a flat check to hit a [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) creature, and you have to succeed at only a DC 5 flat check to target a [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) creature. If you hit and deal damage, you can drive the required weapon into a corporeal target, revealing its current position. You Release the weapon, and it becomes lodged in the target. If the target is concealed, other creatures don't need to succeed at a flat check to hit it. If the target is hidden, other creatures have to succeed at only a DC 5 flat check to target it. The creatures need to be able to see your weapon to gain any of these benefits, and the target can't become [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) to anyone who sees your weapon. If the target is [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26), the weapon remains visible while lodged in it.

 This benefit lasts until the weapon is removed from the creature. An adjacent creature or the target can remove the weapon with 2 Interact actions.

This benefit lasts until the weapon is removed from the creature. An adjacent creature or the target can remove the weapon with two Interact actions.

---

When you counter a [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=38) or [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=110) effect, you send it back to destroy its originator. Whenever you succeed at the [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check to Counter Curse, the creature is affected by its own curse or misfortune effect, attempting a saving throw against its own DC if the effect allows a saving throw. In the case of a constant ability, such as a misfortune aura, the creature is affected only until the beginning of its next turn, when the ability reasserts itself.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"

[Reverse Engineer](/Feats.aspx?ID=8555) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 26

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)

</column>

---

You are incredibly skilled at reverse engineering items to learn their formulas, or disassembling them just to disable them. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) checks to reverse engineer a formula from an item. If you get a critical success on your Crafting check, you can opt to both create the formula and reassemble the original item at the same time, leaving you with the formula and the item instead of the formula and raw materials equal to half the item’s value. Furthermore, you can use Crafting instead of [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) to [Disable a Device](/Actions.aspx?ID=2411) or [Pick a Lock](/Actions.aspx?ID=2412).

---

While under the effect of a mutagen, you can metabolize that mutagen’s power to heal yourself. This uses a single action, which has the concentrate and manipulate traits. Once the action is complete, you regain 1d6 Hit Points for every 2 item levels of the mutagen (minimum 1d6), but the mutagen’s duration immediately ends, even if you are under the effect of Persistent Mutagen.

    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Ricochet Legend](/Feats.aspx?ID=3213) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 119

**Prerequisites**
[Ricochet Master](/Feats.aspx?ID=3207)

</column>

---

The more obstacles between you and your target, the deadlier your shots become, as you ricochet off multiple surfaces to hit them. When using Ricochet Shot, your shot can bounce off of any surface within your weapon's first three range increments and the target can't benefit from cover unless they have total cover on all sides.

In addition, a creature must attempt a Will save against your class DC the first time in an encounter you attack it with a Ricochet Shot. If it fails, it's [stunned 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) and is unable to determine where your shot originated.

</column>

---

You adopt a stance designed to rebound your [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=195) weapons back toward you. While you are in this stance, any thrown weapons you use as part of a ranged Strike to deal bludgeoning or slashing damage immediately return to your hand, enabling you to use them for additional Strikes. You must be within the weapon's listed [range increment](/Traits.aspx?ID=248) and have a hand free to catch the weapon. If you make a ranged Strike with a thrown weapon outside of its listed range increment, it instead flies back toward you a number of feet equal to its listed range increment and then falls to the ground.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Ride the Tsunami](/Feats.aspx?ID=4279) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Overflow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=506" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 33

</column>

---

Booming, crashing walls of water, enough to fill a harbor, smash out ahead of you, overwhelming all in their path. The waves move forward in your choice of a 60-foot cone or 120-foot line. If you're in water, you can increase these waves to a 90-foot cone or 180-foot line. Each creature in the area takes 10d10 bludgeoning damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. A creature that fails its save is [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 20 feet (or 40 feet on a critical failure). Any unattended object of 1 Bulk or less in the area is pushed to the far edge of the area. The sheer mass of water extinguishes all non-magical flames in the area.

 As the wave crashes down, you can catch it to your destination. After the impulse deals damage, you can [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39) in a straight line to any point in its area before the water disappears.

    right="Feat 5"

[Right-Hand Blood](/Feats.aspx?ID=2799) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gnoll" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=219" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Mwangi Expanse](/Sources.aspx?ID=89) pg. 113

</column>

---

It's said that the flesh of the right side of a hyena can heal diseases, but that of the left side is poisonous. You can take 1 damage to feed someone blood from your right side and [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=54) or take 2d8 damage to [Treat Disease](/Actions.aspx?ID=55) or [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=57); in either case, you don't need [healer's tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=25), and gain a +1 item bonus. Blood from your left side causes the check to critically fail automatically.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Undine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=314" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 118

---

The water inside you is cold and frozen, like sheets of ice and frigid glaciers. You gain resistance to cold equal to half your level (minimum 1), and you treat [environmental cold effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=642) as if they were one step less severe (incredible cold becomes extreme, extreme cold becomes severe, and so on).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Barbarian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=18" />
<trait label="Druid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=583" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 56

**Prerequisites**
[animal instinct](/Instincts.aspx?ID=1) or [untamed order](/DruidicOrders.aspx?ID=11)

**Requirements**
Your last action dealt piercing or slashing damage using an [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) Strike granted by a [morph](/Traits.aspx?ID=657) or [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670) effect.

</column>

---

You've learned to debilitate your enemies in the same way a hunter tears at their prey. Make an [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) Strike against the same target. If the Strike hits and deals piercing or slashing damage, the target takes an additional 1d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). If you're at least 12th level, increase this to 2d6 persistent bleed damage.

    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Rise, My Creature!](/Feats.aspx?ID=7474) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 94

**Archetype** [Lepidstadt Surgeon](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=302)

**Prerequisites**
[Lepidstadt Surgeon Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7472)

</column>

---

You have created life! You have usurped the power of the gods themselves! You gain a [prototype construct companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=1600) pieced together from corpses and animated by chemicals or Stasian technology. You use Medicine in place of Crafting to Repair your construct or rebuild it if it's been destroyed. Your creation has an affinity for the lightning that brought it to life. When your construct companion takes electricity damage, it gains a +1 circumstance bonus to its Athletics skill checks until the end of its next turn.

Although the coils or alchemical residue make it obvious to you and those with similar training that your creation is not undead, others must generally succeed at a DC 15 Crafting, Medicine, or Religion check to verify those claims with [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367).

<title level="2">Rise, My Creature! leads to...</title>
[Let my Creature Live!](/Feats.aspx?ID=7476)

    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Rising Hurricane](/Feats.aspx?ID=4307) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=5" />
<trait label="Composite" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=501" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Overflow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=506" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 37

</column>

---

A hurricane lifts your enemies into the air before bringing them crashing down in a bloody rain. Your hurricane appears in a cylinder that's 40 feet tall, has a 30-foot diameter, and is within 120 feet. All creatures in the area take 2d6 bludgeoning damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save against your class DC. Lift any creature that fails its save to any height you choose within the area, move it up to 5 feet in any direction, then drop it. It takes falling damage normally unless it has a fly Speed.

---
**Level (+3)** The rain damage increases by 1d6, and the cylinder's height increases by 5 feet.

Your surgery can bring a patient back from the brink of death, but might push them over the edge. If you do, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) check to Treat Wounds, and if you roll a success, you get a critical success instead.

---

You learn the _[freedom](/Rituals.aspx?ID=193)_ ritual. If you spend an additional [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) while casting it, you reduce its casting time to 1 hour, and both the primary and secondary casters attempt their corresponding skill checks at mythic proficiency. If you would critically fail the ritual, you fail instead. Additionally, you gain the [_unimpeded stride_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1806) and [_word of freedom_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1807) domain spells. These are focus spells, granting you a focus pool of 2 Focus Points or expanding that pool if you already have one. You can Refocus while you meditate on the concepts of freedom and liberty. (For more on focus spells, see [here](/Rules.aspx?ID=2228).)

fields.text: Feat 14 Rites of Liberation Mythic Source War of Immortals pg. 123 Archetype Broken Chain Prerequisites Broken Chain Dedication You learn the freedom ritual. If you spend an additional Mythic Point while casting it, you reduce its casting time to 1 hour, and both the primary and secondary casters attempt their corresponding skill checks at mythic proficiency. If you would critically fail the ritual, you fail instead. Additionally, you gain the unimpeded stride and word of freedom domain spells. These are focus spells, granting you a focus pool of 2 Focus Points or expanding that pool if you already have one. You can Refocus while you meditate on the concepts of freedom and liberty. (For more on focus spells, see here.)

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 105

---

You can adapt your patron's power to transform other creatures into forms more befitting their behavior or your whims. Your familiar learns [_baleful polymorph_](/Spells.aspx?ID=17), even if baleful polymorph isn't on your tradition's spell list. By spending 10 minutes in communion with your familiar, you can replace one spell of 6th level or higher you've prepared in one of your witch spell slots with a _baleful polymorph_ spell of the same level.

>
[Ritualist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2041) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 187

**Archetype** [Ritualist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=72)

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), Expert in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), Expert in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or Expert in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

</column>

---

You have begun to master the difficult art of casting [rituals](/Rules.aspx?ID=777). You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to all primary checks to perform a ritual. You learn two [uncommon](/Traits.aspx?ID=159) [rituals](/Rituals.aspx) with a level no higher than half your level; you must meet all prerequisites for casting the ritual to choose it. At 8th level and every 4 levels thereafter, you learn another uncommon ritual with a level no higher than half your level and for which you meet the prerequisites. You can cast these as the primary caster, but you can't teach them to anyone else or allow someone else to serve as primary caster unless they know the ritual as well.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the ritualist archetype. If you retrain out of this feat, you lose the rituals learned from it.

<title level="2">Ritualist Dedication leads to...</title>
[Efficient Rituals](/Feats.aspx?ID=2044), [Flexible Ritualist](/Feats.aspx?ID=2042), [Resourceful Ritualist](/Feats.aspx?ID=2043)

Webbing sprouts on your legs and tail as you shift to a more aquatic form. You can cast [_feet to fins_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1525) as an innate divine spell once per day. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4), [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7), and [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) as long as you have the [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10), or [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) conditions. You also gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3), [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15), and [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) checks as long as you have the [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24), [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35), or [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) conditions.

</title>

<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 292

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) [Rivethun](/Deities.aspx?ID=388) is a philosophy which characters may choose as their religion. Doing so fulfills the “follower of Rivethun” access condition._

**Archetype** [Rivethun Emissary](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=308)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39); Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

**Access**
Followers of Rivethun have access to this feat.

</column>

---

You’re a practicing Rivethun emissary, skilled at interacting and bonding with the spirits of living creatures. You become an expert in Diplomacy and Religion. You also gain the Bond with Spirit activity and the [_entreat spirit_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2432) focus spell. If you don’t already have one, you gain a [focus pool](/Rules.aspx?ID=285), which you can regain using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=2621) activity to nurture your personal well of spiritual power. Your Rivethun focus spells are [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spells; when you gain this feat, you become trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for Rivethun focus spells is Wisdom.

Bond with Spirit ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [exploration](/Traits.aspx?ID=595)) You can forge a spiritual bond with a creature that is at least friendly toward you or with a terrain that you’re currently in. Forming this bond takes 10 minutes, during which time you must remain adjacent to the creature or within that terrain. If the creature is intelligent, this also requires that creature’s consent, and that intelligent creature can choose to sever this bond with you at any time as a free action, which has the concentrate trait. This bond lasts as long as you are within a mile of the creature or terrain, until you use Bond with Spirit again, or until you make your daily preparations. You must be Bonded with a Spirit to cast the entreat spirit focus spell.

<title level="2">Rivethun Emissary Dedication leads to...</title>
[Consult the Spirits (Rivethun Emissary)](/Feats.aspx?ID=7577), [Domain Spirit](/Feats.aspx?ID=7573), [Emissary Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=7572), [Kaleidoscopic Entreaty](/Feats.aspx?ID=7574), [Manifold Conduit](/Feats.aspx?ID=7578), [Rivethun Devotion](/Feats.aspx?ID=7575)

**Prerequisites**

**Access**
Followers of Rivethun have access to this feat.

</column>

---

You’re a practicing Rivethun invoker, able to enter a trance that connects you physically and mentally to surrounding spirits. You become an expert in Athletics and Religion. You also gain the [Diehard](/Feats.aspx?ID=5140) general feat and the Enter Spirit Trance ability. 

**Enter Spirit Trance** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) You enter a self-imposed trance that helps you push the physical limits of your body. You gain a number of temporary Hit Points equal to your level plus your Constitution modifier. The trance lasts for 1 minute, until you fall [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), or until you [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) it, whichever comes first. While in this trance, you gain a +1 status bonus to Fortitude and Will saving throws and your melee [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) deal 1 additional [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage. Other abilities may require you to be in a spirit trance. When the trace ends, you lose any remaining [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) from Enter Spirit Trance, and you can’t Enter a Spirit Trance for 1 minute.

<title level="2">Rivethun Invoker Dedication leads to...</title>
[Defy Sorrow](/Feats.aspx?ID=7585), [Invoke Defense](/Feats.aspx?ID=7584), [Invoke Movement](/Feats.aspx?ID=7586), [Invoke Offense](/Feats.aspx?ID=7582), [Leverage Anguish](/Feats.aspx?ID=7583), [One with the Spirits](/Feats.aspx?ID=7587)

Your innate connection to stone makes you adept at moving across uneven surfaces. You can ignore difficult terrain caused by rubble and uneven ground made of stone and earth.     pfs="Standard"
>
[Rock the Boat](/Feats.aspx?ID=9027) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=71" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 93

**Access**
You're from the Shackles

**Trigger**
A creature within your reach causes you to [fall](/Rules.aspx?ID=2352) or knocks you [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).

</column>

---

You know how easy it is for a falling person to cause another to lose their footing at the same time, and how to use that to your advantage. As you fall, you grab onto an enemy using your hands or legs, and pull them down with you. Attempt an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check against the triggering creature’s Reflex DC. On a success, the creature falls with you (though it can still attempt to [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2313)) or is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).

>
[Rogue Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=727) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
<trait label="Multiclass" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=115" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 229

**Archetype** [Rogue](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=10)

**Prerequisites**
Dexterity 14

</column>

---

You gain a skill feat and the rogue’s surprise attack class feature. You become trained in light armor. In addition, you become trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) or [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) plus one skill of your choice; if you are already trained in both Stealth and Thievery, you become trained in an additional skill of your choice. You become trained in rogue class DC.

**Special** You cannot gain another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the rogue archetype.

<title level="2">Rogue Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Trickery](/Feats.aspx?ID=728), [Evasiveness (Rogue)](/Feats.aspx?ID=733), [Skill Mastery (Rogue)](/Feats.aspx?ID=731), [Sneak Attacker](/Feats.aspx?ID=729), [Uncanny Dodge](/Feats.aspx?ID=732)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Roiling Mudslide](/Feats.aspx?ID=4308) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Composite" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=501" />
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 37

</column>

---

You form water and earth into a mudslide that smashes your opponents and coats them in mud. Each creature in a 30-foot cone takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save against your class DC. A creature that fails is also [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 5 feet (or 10 feet on a critical failure) and coated in mud until the end of its next turn. While coated in mud, the creature falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) at the end of its movement any time it ends a [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114) action other than a Crawl or Step. The creature can attempt an [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) check or Reflex save against your class DC, avoiding the fall if it succeeds.

---
**Level (+4)** The damage increases by 1d8.

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 141 **Frequency** once per 10 minutes **Prerequisites** [bones mystery](/Mysteries.aspx?ID=14) or [lore mystery](/Mysteries.aspx?ID=18) --- You roll a handful of bones to learn (or perhaps influence) the future course of events. Roll 1d4 and use the corresponding result below. Whenever you Roll the Bones of Fate, any effects from a previous usage immediately end.
**1 Good** You or an ally within 30 feet can roll twice on your next attack roll or skill check, taking the higher result. This is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect.
**2 Bad** One creature you are observing within 30 feet must succeed at a Will save against your spell DC; on a failure, the target must roll twice on their next attack roll or skill check that takes at least one action to perform, taking the lower result. This is a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect.
**3 Mixed** You gain the benefits of rolling both a 1 and a 2.
**4 Cursed Possibilities** Your attempts to meddle in the forces of prophecy bring dire consequences for all. Every creature within 30 feet of you when you perform the augury rolls twice on their next attack roll or skill check that takes at least one action to perform; if the highest number rolled is odd, they take the lower result, and if the highest number rolled is even, they take the higher result. If they took the lower result, this effect has the misfortune trait for them, and if they took the higher result, it has the fortune trait.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Roll with It (Goblin)](/Feats.aspx?ID=1009) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Goblin" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=81" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 39

**Prerequisites**
[Unbreakable Goblin](/Heritages.aspx?ID=20) heritage; [Bouncy Goblin](/Feats.aspx?ID=999)

**Trigger**
A foe hits you with a melee weapon or unarmed attack.

</column>

---

When you take a big hit, your foe bounces you around like a rubber ball, but you escape the worst of the blow. Your foe can move you any distance of its choice up to 30 feet in a direction of its choice (this is not forced movement, and it triggers reactions as normal). You fall prone and are stunned 1. Attempt a DC 6 flat check. On a success, you take minimum damage from the attack, and on a critical success, if the attack was a critical hit, you don’t take double damage from the critical hit.

Attempt a Reflex save using 10 + the giant's attack bonus as the save DC. If the result allows you to Stride as part of the reaction, you may instead [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39) if you have the corresponding movement type. **Critical Success** The attack misses you (or if the attack was a critical hit, it becomes a regular hit). You can Stride up to 10 feet as part of the reaction; if you do so, the reaction gains the [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114) trait.
**Success** The attack deals half damage. You can Stride up to 5 feet as part of the reaction, but you must end this movement adjacent to the triggering giant. If you do so, the reaction gains the move trait.
**Critical Failure** You fail to avoid the attack and are knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) by the blow. Adventuring with Ekundayo **Source** [Kingmaker Companion Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=151) pg. 23 Ekundayo eventually develops his own methods to pursue his favored enemies—giants. Once he gains the Magical Crafting feat at 4th level, he begins to craft specialized ammunition and runes for weapons. As long as his attitude toward the PCs is at least friendly, he shares these discoveries with them, unlocking the following ranger class feats and items as soon as his level equals the level of the feat or item. **Related Feats**: [Giant Hunter](/Feats.aspx?ID=3900), [Giant Slayer](/Feats.aspx?ID=3904), [Hamstringing Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=3902), [The Harder They Fall (Ranger)](/Feats.aspx?ID=3901)

    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Rolling Landing](/Feats.aspx?ID=4124) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 76

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Rolling Landing’s text only affects the reaction used after a fall, not any reaction._

**Prerequisites**
[Cat Fall](/Feats.aspx?ID=765); Trained in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1)

</column>

---

You land with quick rolls that help you keep your momentum. If you [fall](/Rules.aspx?ID=402) more than 5 feet and don't take damage (usually due to treating the fall as a shorter distance), you can use your reaction to immediately enter a short roll when you land and Step. If you are an expert in Acrobatics, you can use your reaction to Step or Stride up to half your Speed. If you're a master in Acrobatics, you can use your reaction to Step or Stride up to your full Speed. If you're legendary in Acrobatics, you don't trigger reactions triggered by movement when you Stride in this way.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Tanuki" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=830" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 68

**Prerequisites**
[Teakettle Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=6934)

**Trigger**
You [Drop Prone](/Actions.aspx?ID=2295) or othwerwise become [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) 

</column>

---

As you fall to the ground, you transform into a white bottle, gourd, or sake jar, then roll away before anyone can pick you up. You [Crawl](/Actions.aspx?ID=2293) up to two times, and your movement doesn’t provoke reactions—you somehow always roll just out of reach. When you come to a stop, you return to your tanuki form, face down on the ground.

    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Root to Life](/Feats.aspx?ID=3702) <actions string="Single Action or Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Esoterica" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=427" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 42

</column>

---

Marigold, spider lily, pennyroyal—many primal traditions connect flowers and plants with the boundary between life and death, and you can leverage this association to keep an ally on this side of the line. You place a small plant or similar symbol on an adjacent [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=11) creature, immediately stabilizing them; the creature is no longer dying and is instead [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) at 0 Hit Points.

 If you spend 2 actions instead of 1, you empower the act further by uttering a quick folk blessing to chase away ongoing pain, adding the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) trait to the action. When you do so, attempt flat checks to remove each source of [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) affecting the target; due to the particularly effective assistance, the DC is 10 instead of the usual 15.

>
[Rope Mastery](/Feats.aspx?ID=2737) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #167: Ready? Fight!](/Sources.aspx?ID=86) pg. 76

**Archetype** [Golden League Xun](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=93)

**Prerequisites**
[Golden League Xun Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2734); Expert in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3)

</column>

---

Ropes are your tool of choice, and you deploy them in versatile ways. When [Climbing](/Actions.aspx?ID=33) a rope, you move 5 more feet on a success and 10 more feet on a critical success, to a maximum of your Speed. This additional movement stacks with the effects of [Quick Climb](/Feats.aspx?ID=821).

 In addition, you can use a rope to hamper your foes. When holding a rope, you can attempt an Athletics check to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41), [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35), or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) a creature up to 10 feet away instead of only adjacent creatures. If you critically fail such a check while holding a rope, you can drop the rope to take the effects of a failure instead of a critical failure.

You run and climb across ropes and rigging almost as easily as on the ground. You gain a climb Speed of 15 feet, but only on ship's rigging or similar ropes. You aren't [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) while Climbing or Balancing on a rope.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 84

**Archetype** [Rose Warden](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=378)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48); you worship [Milani](/Deities.aspx?ID=352)

</column>

---

As a follower of the Everbloom, you stand up against tyranny and oppression, understanding that revolution against an unjust ruler must sometimes be enacted in secret. You become trained in Deception. If you're already trained in Deception, you become an expert in your choice of Deception or Stealth. When you get a critical success to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) to a figure of authority, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude DC and saving throws against being [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63), [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64), [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81), or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) by that figure of authority for 24 hours.

 You add the edicts and anathema of Milani to your own (see sidebar). Failing to uphold edicts or committing acts that violate the anathema result in you losing access to any abilities granted by this archetype, as determined by your GM. You can regain these lost abilities through the atone ritual as normal.

<title level="2">Rose Warden Dedication leads to...</title>
[Blessed Thorn Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=8907), [Holy Bloom](/Feats.aspx?ID=8908), [Liberated Mind](/Feats.aspx?ID=8911), [Rise Up!](/Feats.aspx?ID=8914), [Unbalancing Appearance](/Feats.aspx?ID=8909), [Unfettering Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=8910), [Wall of Roses](/Feats.aspx?ID=8912)

You enter a stance that makes it difficult to move around you. Each square adjacent to you becomes difficult terrain that matches the terrain attunement you gained (rime forms in an arctic terrain, momentary undergrowth shoots up in a forest terrain, and so on). You ignore this difficult terrain.

 This stance ends if you move into a different type of terrain.

---

Your elven lineage is subtle enough that you look barely different from other humans, and you’ve learned to use that to your advantage. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) (or another skill of your choice, if you were already trained in Deception). You gain a +4 circumstance bonus to Impersonate checks to pretend you aren’t a half-elf. Observers are never granted circumstance bonuses to Perception checks due to you Impersonating a full-blooded human, and you never take circumstance penalties due to you Impersonating a full-blooded human.

**Special** You can take this feat only at 1st level, and you can’t retrain out of this feat or into this feat.

The spirit within your pusaka resonates with other magical items in your possession. Your pusaka gains the following activation.

**Activate—Replenish Heirloom** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your pusaka uses its power to spark one of your depleted magic items to life. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Rouse the Forest's Fury](/Feats.aspx?ID=4294) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Overflow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=506" />
<trait label="Plant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=125" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 35

</column>

---

Terrifying trees attack your enemies. Three Large trees appear in unoccupied spaces within 500 feet, at least 15 feet from one another. Each tree has AC 40, Fortitude +33, Reflex +24, Will +30, and 200 HP. The trees can flank, but are unable to move. When the trees appear, each makes a Strike; they share a multiple attack penalty. The tree's melee Strike is a branch that has reach 10 feet; on a hit, the target is [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) by the tree ([Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) DC 40). The ranged Strike is a hurled fruit, gourd, seed, or stone with a range increment of 60 feet. Either Strike has a +30 attack modifier and deals 4d10+9 bludgeoning damage.

 The trees last until the end of your next turn, and you can Sustain the impulse. Each time you Sustain the impulse, you can have one tree make a Strike.

---
**Level (20th)** The attack modifier is +32 and the Strike damage is 5d10+9.

You were born to a jiang-shi, one of the so-called hopping vampires found most often in Tian-Xia. Your skin develops a malleable, rubbery quality. You gain resistance to bludgeoning damage equal to 2 + your number of class feats from the oozemorph archetype. You also gain resistance equal to twice that amount to extra damage from critical hits; if the resistance is greater than the extra damage, it reduces the extra damage to 0 but doesn't reduce the attack's normal damage.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Fists of the Ruby Phoenix</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Sorcerer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=148" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #168: King of the Mountain](/Sources.aspx?ID=87) pg. 76

**Frequency**
once per day

**Trigger**
You would be reduced to 0 Hit Points.

</column>

---

In a burst of flame, you return to health like a [phoenix](/Monsters.aspx?ID=330) rising from the ashes. Change your current Hit Points to 30 and cast a 6th-level [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=119) centered on yourself. This fireball doesn't affect you. Your hair turns brilliant red for 1 hour.

 If you haven't used Ruby Resurrection and you die, you stay in initiative order and Ruby Resurrection triggers automatically at the start of your next turn, bringing you back to life at 0 HP before having its normal effects. This happens only if there are some remains to resurrect; for instance, if you were killed by [_disintegrate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=76) you wouldn't return.

**Special** This feat has the trait corresponding to the tradition of spells you cast.

<title level="2">Capstone Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #168: King of the Mountain](/Sources.aspx?ID=87) pg. 75

Player characters can select one of the following new class feats for their 20th-level class feat upon entering the _Glass Lighthouse_ or by meditating on the cushion in area H4.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 52

**Archetype** [Swordmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=33)

**Prerequisites**
[Swordmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1139); Master in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16)

</column>

---

You've studied survival skills with the School of Swords experts and are comfortable spending long periods of time in the wilderness. You don't get fatigued more quickly due to precipitation during overland travel, though you can otherwise be fatigued as normal. You can go 3 days + your Constitution modifier without water before you take damage from thirst and you can go 5 days + your Constitution modifier without food before you take damage from [starvation](/Rules.aspx?ID=537).

The villain of the tale you've spun makes an attack roll with a given weapon or unarmed attack, uses a particular special ability (such as a Breath Weapon), or Casts a Spell against the hero, and they used that same attack, special ability, or spell against the hero on the previous turn.

**Requirements**
You have Spun a Tale.

</column>

---

Heroes learn from their previous failures, often succeeding on the third attempt. You narrate a tale of the hero's success, granting them a +2 circumstance bonus to their AC or saving throw against the triggering effect. If the villain has used the same effect against the hero on both of their last two turns, and you used Rule of Three on that effect last turn as well, the bonus increases to +4.

</title>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 48

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45)

</column>

---

You practice the lost art of using music to guide your runecarving, singing the runes into existence as much as crafting them. You can use Performance instead of [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) when attempting Crafting checks related to runes.

Once per 10 minutes, you can [Trace a Rune](/Actions.aspx?ID=4264) with song alone. When you do, you use the 2-action version of Trace Rune as a single action without needing an [artisan's toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2703), and you remove the action's [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) trait. You don't need to be able to move your hands when Tracing a Rune using song, but you do need to be able to sing in a clear voice.

<title level="2">Rune-Singer leads to...</title>
[Prodigal Rune-Singer](/Feats.aspx?ID=9200), [Song of Glorious Invocation](/Feats.aspx?ID=9183)

---

Whether through blood (if you’re Varisian, Shoanti, or New Thassilonian) or by exposure to rune magic, you have become runescarred, with visible, glowing runes on your body in the form of tattoos or scars. You might have possessed these marks before gaining the archetype, but you only truly became runescarred when you chose to study and tap into the runes’ power. You become an expert in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) and you also become trained in Thassilon [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8), or an expert in Thassilon Lore if you were already trained in it.

 Choose one cantrip from the [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1) list. One of the runes on your body corresponds to the chosen cantrip, and you can cast the chosen cantrip as an innate arcane spell.

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the runescarred archetype.

<title level="2">Runescarred Dedication leads to...</title>

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 90

**Archetype** [Runesmith](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=388)

**Prerequisites**
Intelligence +2

</column>

---

You become trained in runesmith [class DC](/Rules.aspx?ID=2051) and [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37). You gain a [runic repertoire](/RunesmithRunes.aspx) with two 1st-level runes of your choice. You choose these from the common runes on the rune list as well as uncommon or rarer runes you have access to. 

You can etch runes. An etched rune is carved, inked, or branded; this application does not damage the creature or item. Etching a rune requires an artisan's toolkit. Your magic can sustain up to one etched rune at a time. If you're at least 9th level, increase the maximum number of etched runes you can sustain at a time to 2, and if you're at least 17th level, increase it to 3. You can etch any number of runes up to your maximum during your daily preparations or by spending 10 minutes in exploration mode. Your etched runes remain indefinitely until they're expended or removed or until you etch more runes than your maximum, which causes your oldest rune to fade. Additionally, you gain the Solitary Invocation action. 

**Solitary Invocation** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([invocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=956), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [runesmith](/Traits.aspx?ID=952)) You utter the name of one of your runes within 30 feet, which blazes with power, applying the effect in its Invocation entry. An invoked rune then fades away, its task complete.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Runic Correspondence](/Feats.aspx?ID=9201) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Runesmith" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=952" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 51

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), Master in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), Master in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or Master in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

</column>

---

You can write a message that travels long distances at the speed of thought. Once per day, you can take 1 minute to write a message of 25 words or fewer anywhere that can, at least momentarily, hold writing (such as on a piece of parchment, drawn in the sand, or lightly scratched onto soft metal). When you are finished, mentally picture one creature you know well. If the target creature is on the same plane as you, your message appears in their line of sight on any surface that can hold writing. It can be seen by only the target, and the target can read the message even if you don’t share a language. The message disappears once the target reads it, but the creature can respond by spending 1 minute to write their own message of 25 words or fewer in the same way. You instantly receive that message when it is finished, and you can read it even if you don’t share a language.

If you spend 10 minutes writing your message instead, you can include a rune from your runic repertoire. If the target is willing, after reading your message, you Trace the Rune on the target to last for up to 10 minutes. When you receive the creature’s reply, you can Invoke that Rune as a free action.

fields.text: Feat 10 Runic Correspondence Runesmith Source Impossible Magic pg. 51 Prerequisites Master in Arcana, Master in Nature, Master in Occultism, or Master in Religion You can write a message that travels long distances at the speed of thought. Once per day, you can take 1 minute to write a message of 25 words or fewer anywhere that can, at least momentarily, hold writing (such as on a piece of parchment, drawn in the sand, or lightly scratched onto soft metal). When you are finished, mentally picture one creature you know well. If the target creature is on the same plane as you, your message appears in their line of sight on any surface that can hold writing. It can be seen by only the target, and the target can read the message even if you don’t share a language. The message disappears once the target reads it, but the creature can respond by spending 1 minute to write their own message of 25 words or fewer in the same way. You instantly receive that message when it is finished, and you can read it even if you don’t share a language. If you spend 10 minutes writing your message instead, you can include a rune from your runic repertoire. If the target is willing, after reading your message, you Trace the Rune on the target to last for up to 10 minutes. When you receive the creature’s reply, you can Invoke that Rune as a free action.

---

By drawing your favorite rune in your flesh, you know you’ll never be without it. Choose one rune you know, which you apply as a tattoo to your body. The rune is always etched on your body and does not count toward your maximum limit of etched runes. You can invoke this rune like any of your other runes, but once invoked, the rune fades significantly and is drained of power until your next daily preparations. 

You can magically alter your runic tattoo to change it to another rune you know (or remove it altogether) with 1 day of downtime.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Highhelm](/Sources.aspx?ID=204) pg. 111

**Archetype** [Stalwart Defender](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=205)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Stalwart Defender Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=4172)

**Requirements**
You are in Tenacious Stance.

</column>

---

Every dwarf knows that the rock they walk upon can be either a best friend or a treacherous path. With a heavy impact of your armored heel, you crack the ground underneath you. The ground within a 10-foot emanation becomes [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453). If you are a master or better in the armor you are wearing, this becomes greater difficult terrain. The cracked ground settles and reverts to normal terrain after 1 minute.

**Special** At 16th level, you can take this feat again. If you do, you can use it once per hour instead of once per day.

    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Rushing Goat Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=7106) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=656" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=701" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 119

**Archetype** [Martial Artist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=255) (Level 4)

**Requirements**
You're [unarmored](/Armor.aspx?ID=38).

</column>

---

You enter the stance of an unruly goat, lowering your body and preparing to butt heads with your foes. The only [Strikes](/Rules.aspx?ID=2895) you can make are ramming horn attacks. These strikes deal 1d8 bludgeoning damage, are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group, and have the [forceful](/Traits.aspx?ID=611), [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661), [shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380), and [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) traits. When you make a ramming horn attack and your previous action was to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), Stride, or [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298), you gain a circumstance bonus to damage equal to the number of weapon damage dice. You can make ramming horn Strikes while Climbing even if you don’t have a free hand.

<title level="2">Rushing Goat Stance leads to...</title>
[Five-gods Ram](/Feats.aspx?ID=7112), [Momentous Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=7109)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=541" />
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=590" />
<trait label="Linguistic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=642" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 58

**Archetype** [Kitharodian Actor](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=301)

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
[Kitharodian Actor Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7456)

</column>

---

You were once cast in the role of Daronlyr XII, one of Taldor’s most ambitious rulers who slew his cousin to seize the crown, yet somehow still managed to convince the entire Ulfen Guard to swear loyalty to him simply through his powers of oration. You attempt a Performance check to launch into a powerful monologue, pulling lines from Daronlyr’s playbook to win respect from everyone around you, even your enemies. The DC of this check is a [hard difficulty DC](/Rules.aspx?ID=2627) of your level. On a success, any hostile creatures within 20 feet take a –2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls and spell attack rolls that target you until the beginning of your next turn, and any allies within 20 feet are quickened until the beginning of your next turn. The additional action can be only used to Strike or Stride.

    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sacral Lord](/Feats.aspx?ID=3837) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=24" />
<trait label="Oracle" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=319" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 177

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) or Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

</column>

---

By right of ritual or sheer stubbornness, you have claimed rulership of the land. Claim a defined territory, such as a small section of forest or river, or a district of a larger city. Within its borders, you can cast [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=66), [_guidance_](/Spells.aspx?ID=142), and [_sigil_](/Spells.aspx?ID=286) as innate divine cantrips, and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) on creatures that have the [celestial](/Traits.aspx?ID=23), [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=70), [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69), [monitor](/Traits.aspx?ID=111), or [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=149) traits.

**Special** You and your land are linked. Changes to one mirror themselves on the other—if you're depressed, gray rain and clammy mist might set in. These effects have no immediate mechanical impact, but they might give clues about problems afflicting the land.

<title level="2">Sacral Lord leads to...</title>
[Sacral Monarch](/Feats.aspx?ID=3838)

[Sacral Lord](/Feats.aspx?ID=8478) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=811" />
<trait label="Oracle" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=817" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=293) pg. 177

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) or Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

</column>

---

By right of ritual or sheer stubbornness, you have claimed rulership of the land. Claim a defined territory, such as a small section of forest or river, or a district of a larger city. Within its borders, you can cast [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485), [_guidance_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1549), and [_sigil_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1673) as innate divine cantrips, and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) on creatures that have the [celestial](/Traits.aspx?ID=551), [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600), [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=599), [monitor](/Traits.aspx?ID=655), or [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) traits.

**Special** You and your land are linked. Changes to one mirror themselves on the other—if you're depressed, gray rain and clammy mist might set in. These effects have no immediate mechanical impact, but they might give clues about problems afflicting the land.

You are a great warrior that can stand strong against the fiercest opponents to your cause. You gain resistance 10 to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage caused by creatures and effects opposed to your tenets (unholy creatures for tenets of good, holy creatures for tenets of evil, and so on). <trait label="Consecration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=34" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 116

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Prerequisites**
[harmful font or healing font](/Classes.aspx?ID=5)

</column>

---

You pray continuously for 1 minute to call a subtle shadow of your deity’s realm over a 30-foot burst centered on you. It lasts for 10 minutes, and a creature that remains in the area for the entire 10 minutes regains Hit Points equal to your level. If you have a healing font, this activity has the healing and vitality traits and heals living creatures.

If you have a harmful font, this activity has the healing and void traits and heals undead creatures (or other creatures with void healing). Clerics with Versatile Font can choose either or both. It can’t damage creatures in any case.

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 25 **Archetype** [Hallowed Necromancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=172) **Prerequisites** [Hallowed Necromancer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3459) --- Add [_chill touch_](/Spells.aspx?ID=35), [_death ward_](/Spells.aspx?ID=64), [_disrupt undead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=79), [_disrupting weapons_](/Spells.aspx?ID=80), [_holy cascade_](/Spells.aspx?ID=151), [_magic stone_](/Spells.aspx?ID=703), and [_sunburst_](/Spells.aspx?ID=326) to your spell list. These are all [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117) spells for you, even if they normally have a different spell school. You can either prepare these spells or add them to your repertoire just like the spells normally on your tradition's spell list. When you gain this feat, you can retrain existing spells to replace them with ones on this list. In addition, your knowledge of the conduits to the [Positive Energy Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=3) allows you more flexibility with these spells. Choose one of these two benefits.
  • If you're a prepared spellcaster, you can spend 10 minutes to replace one of the spells you've prepared with a spell of the same level from the list of sacred spells. You can do this while [Refocusing](/Actions.aspx?ID=71).
  • If you're a spontaneous spellcaster with the signature spells class feature, add two of the spells from the list of sacred spells to your repertoire. They are signature spells for you, in addition to your normal signature spells. When you gain the ability to cast a new level of spells, you can choose to switch the spells from this feat to any other spells from the list.

    right="Feat 4"

[Sacred Wilds Oath](/Feats.aspx?ID=7022) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 92

**Archetype** [Spirit Warrior](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=274)

**Prerequisites**
[Spirit Warrior Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7020)

</column>

---

You’ve sworn an oath to protect the holy places within nature and the spirits that dwell within, from ancient trees to primordial wild guardians. You can use [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) on animals and to make very simple [Requests](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) of them. In most cases, wild animals will give you time to make your case. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Diplomacy checks to Make an Impression when interacting with a [beast](/Traits.aspx?ID=547), [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=599), or [kami](/Traits.aspx?ID=354). You gain the following edict. 

**Edict** You must aid any animal or nature spirit in need unless it violates your other tenets or puts someone else at risk of immediate harm.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 22

</column>

---

Elements are wild and dangerous, but you've found ways to reduce their risk. When you [Channel Elements](/Actions.aspx?ID=2124) or use a [stance](/Traits.aspx?ID=152) [impulse](/Traits.aspx?ID=502) that affects your kinetic aura, you can designate a number of creatures up to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1 creature). Choose whether they are immune to the benefits of your kinetic aura or immune to its damage and drawbacks. You don't have to be able to see a creature to designate it, nor does it need to be in your kinetic aura, but you can't designate a creature that's [unnoticed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=41) by you.

 In addition, you gain the Pacifying Infusion action.

 **Pacifying Infusion** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([infusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=503)) If your next action is an impulse, it gains the [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188) trait. If it has an area, you can exclude creatures you've designated with Safe Elements from its effects.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Safe House](/Feats.aspx?ID=2086) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 196

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) A vigilante's Safe House, can be located in any city or near any lodge they have received a Pathfinder briefing. A vigilante can use their downtime to relocate their safe house. A vigilante can use their safe house only if it is in the town or location where their current adventure is taking place._

**Archetypes** [Vigilante](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=80), [Bellflower Tiller](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=400) (Level 4)

**Prerequisites**
[Vigilante Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2083)

</column>

---

You establish a safe house—a secure space in which to hide your secrets from the outside world. This safe house is roughly the size of a 10-foot cube. It's in a location you have access to, and it can be part of a larger building or structure, like a hidden room or an underground cave. The safe house protects objects and people inside it from magical detection. This has the effects of [_nondetection_](/Spells.aspx?ID=209), using your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) modifier for the [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC and half your level rounded up for the counteract level. Setting up or moving your safe house takes a week of downtime. The size of the safe house expands to four 10-foot cubes if you're an expert in Deception, eight cubes if you're a master, and 16 cubes if you're legendary.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"

[Samsaran Weapon Memory](/Feats.aspx?ID=6899) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Samsaran" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=828" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 56

</column>

---

The training of your past lives and even of those of samsarans who came before is deep-seated and guides your movements in combat. Choose two weapons with an ancestry trait from two different common [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=628) ancestries, or other ancestries you have access to. You gain access to your chosen weapons. You have familiarity with these weapons—for the purposes of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons. 

At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its [critical specialization](/Rules.aspx?ID=2203) effect.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 18"
    pfs=""
>
[Sanctified Relic](/Feats.aspx?ID=7400) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 132

**Archetype** [Godling](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=293)

**Prerequisites**
[Godling Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7392)

</column>

---

You fill an item with your divine power, granting the wearer your blessings. When you take this feat, choose two attributes (one of which must be your key attribute) as your divine attributes and either [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) or [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) sanctification; if you have the holy or unholy trait through a class feature or other ability, you must choose that same trait. As part of your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575), you can touch one worn magical item that doesn’t have the [apex](/Traits.aspx?ID=532) trait. It gains the apex trait until your next daily preparations, and increases the modifier of one of your divine attributes (chosen during your preparations) by 1 or to a total of +4, whichever is higher. In addition, the item grants the wearer the holy or unholy trait as chosen by you. A character can benefit from only one apex item at a time, as normal. You can’t wear this apex item, but your hierophant can. 

If you spend 1 Mythic Point when you create this apex item, it increases the wearer’s modifiers of both of your divine attributes by 1 or to a total of +4, whichever is higher. This is an exception to the usual limit for apex items.

    right="Feat 7"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sanctify Water](/Feats.aspx?ID=1185) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Gods & Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=17) pg. 105

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) When using Sanctify Water use your proficiency with simple weapons to determine your attack bonus when throwing the blessed container of water. If you give the container to another character for them to throw, they use their proficiency with improvised weapons instead._

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13); good or evil deity

</column>

---

You imbue water with your deity’s blessing. Choose a container of water on your person that is of light Bulk. For 1 round, if you or an ally throw this container at a foe, it has the damaging effects of [holy water](/Equipment.aspx?ID=245) (if you follow a good deity) or [unholy water](/Equipment.aspx?ID=248) (if you follow an evil deity). The water’s transient power doesn’t make it gain any value, allow it to be used to supply the cost for a spell or ritual, and so on. If you have legendary proficiency in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13), you can sanctify three containers held by you or allies within your reach instead of one.

<title

    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sanctify Water](/Feats.aspx?ID=6502) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=615" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 233

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46); you follow a deity with “holy” or “unholy” sanctification

</column>

---

You imbue water with your deity's blessing. Choose a container of water with light Bulk possessed by you or an ally within your reach. Until the end of your next turn, it becomes [holy water](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3001) or [unholy water](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3006). You can choose holy water if your deity allows holy sanctification, unholy water if your deity allows unholy sanctification, or either if your deity allows both sanctifications. This is a temporary effect and doesn't impart monetary value or allow the water to be used for costs of rituals or the like. If you're a master in Religion, you can sanctify two containers when you take this action, and if you're legendary, you can sanctify three.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sand Snatcher](/Feats.aspx?ID=4227) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 26

</column>

---

A figure of sand with grasping arms arises in an unoccupied square within 30 feet. You can choose to make it Small or Medium size, and it can flank. When the sand snatcher appears, you can have it attempt to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) one creature adjacent to it that's no more than one size larger than it. This Grapple uses your impulse attack roll instead of an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check and shares your multiple attack penalty. The sand snatcher lasts until the end of your next turn, and you can Sustain the impulse up to 1 minute. Each time you Sustain the impulse, you can have the sand snatcher either Grapple again or [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=93), [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=33), or Stride up to 20 feet. Attempts to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) its grasp use your class DC.

---
**Level (10th)** You can also choose Large size.

**Level (14th)** You can also choose Large or Huge size.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Sanguimancer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7764) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Shades of Blood</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #213: Thirst for Blood](/Sources.aspx?ID=257) pg. 84

**Archetype** [Sanguimancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=321)

</column>

---

The life essence in your blood recovers naturally over time. You gain a special type of [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) called sanguimancy Hit Points that follow the normal rules for temporary Hit Points with two exceptions: you can spend them to power some sanguimancy feats, and you can never have a greater number of sanguimancy Hit Points than double your level. 

After a full 8-hour rest, you gain sanguimancy HP equal to your level that last for 8 hours. If someone successfully restores HP to you with Treat Wounds, you also gain 1 sanguimancy HP for every 10 Hit Points recovered (minimum 1 sanguimancy HP).

**Special** Sanguimancer feats have the trait matching your spellcaster tradition; if you don't have one, choose [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) or [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) when you select the Sanguimancer Dedication.

<title level="2">Sanguimancer Dedication leads to...</title>
[Blood Shield](/Feats.aspx?ID=7765), [Exsanguinate](/Feats.aspx?ID=7766), [Transfusion](/Feats.aspx?ID=7767), [Venipuncture](/Feats.aspx?ID=7768)

    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sanguine Evasion](/Feats.aspx?ID=9015) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=139" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 65

**Access**
member of the Red Mantis assassins

**Trigger**
You’re reduced to 0 Hit Points and are not already [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=99).

</column>

---

You avoid death by turning into a spray of red mist. You remain at 1 Hit Point and transform into a vaporous state with the effects of [_vapor form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1738), except your [fly Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350) is equal to your land Speed and you can occupy the same space as another creature. Creatures in the same space as you in this form are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62). 

You can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) this form, returning to your normal form with 1 Hit Point and becoming wounded 1. If you don’t Dismiss this form within 1 minute, you return to your normal form with 0 Hit Points and become [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) 1.

<title

    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sanguine Mastery](/Feats.aspx?ID=9142) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Necromancer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=950" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 39

**Prerequisites**
[blood grim fascination](/GrimFascinations.aspx?ID=1)

</column>

---

Your mastery over the intricacies of your fascination has allowed you to infuse your own blood with additional healing properties while increasing your ability to bleed out any foes that stand against you. You gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) to [bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) damage equal to half your level. Additionally, if an enemy within 30 feet of you is bleeding, you gain [fast healing](/Rules.aspx?ID=2322) equal to half your level. This fast healing is deactivated while you have the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition.

In addition, whenever you destroy a thrall, a creature adjacent to the thrall takes 1 persistent bleed damage. If that creature is already taking bleed damage, instead increase its bleed damage by 1. A creature can have its bleed damage increased in this way only once per round.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sanguivolent Roots](/Feats.aspx?ID=4290) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Overflow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=506" />
<trait label="Plant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=125" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 35

</column>

---

Blood-drinking vines grow from the ground in a 15-foot burst within 120 feet. Each living enemy in the area has its blood drained, taking 3d6 piercing damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save against your class DC. Each time the vines drink blood, living creatures in the area who aren't your enemies regain HP equal to half the damage a single creature took; calculate this using the highest damage a single creature took. This is a [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=89) [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) effect. Your enemies with [void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=42) in the area take vitality damage in the same amount as the healing. The vines last until the end of your next turn, and you can Sustain the impulse. The first time you Sustain the impulse on subsequent turns, you can repeat the effect.

---
**Level (+2)** The damage increases by 1d6.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Saoc Astrology](/Feats.aspx?ID=946) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Human" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=90" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 12

**Frequency**
3 times per day

**Access**
Lirgeni nationality

**Requirements**
You must spend 10 minutes just after your daily preparations examining the sky or consulting a star chart or you can’t use this action that day.

</column>

---

The ancient Saoc Brethren were the masters of astrology, and while your knowledge may be but a pale shadow of their wisdom, it still comes in handy. You recall the stars’ predictions about your current situation. If your next action requires you to attempt one or more skill checks, roll 1d8. On a result of 6, 7, or 8, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the first such skill check you attempt. On a 3, 4, or 5, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus. On a 2, you gain nothing. On a 1, you take a –1 circumstance penalty to the skill check.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=139" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 65

**Prerequisites**
trained in [sawtooth sabers](/Weapons.aspx?ID=423)

**Access**
member of the Red Mantis assassins

</column>

---

Your sawtooth saber training enables you to pin down an enemy using your twin blades. Make a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) with each weapon against the same creature. If you deal sneak attack damage, you can immediately attempt to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) the creature, even if you don’t have a hand free. If you dealt damage with both Strikes, your multiple attack penalty is not applied to the Grapple attempt.

**Special** You’re wielding two weapons, at least one of which is a sawtooth saber.

<title level="2">Sawtooth Grapple leads to...</title>
[Cutthroat Grapple](/Feats.aspx?ID=9013)
